#40350. Breaking: This is technically the worst version of GTA 6 that we'll ever play

Breaking: This is technically the worst version of GTA 6 that we'll ever play

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1415 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I've been playing GTA 6 through the morning to try to see what the fuss is about, and now I totally get it.
  • That sounds like an insult, but I mean the exact opposite.
  • I work for PC Gamer, so forgive my snobbery when I say the PC version should be far superior to what we're right now playing on consoles.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've been playing GTA 6 through the morning to try to see what the fuss is about, and now I totally get it. After mere hours in the game, I'm already coming to terms with the scale of it; not just the size of the map, but the attention to detail on every object and interaction. But I have to remind myself, this is sure to be the worst version of GTA 6 we'll ever play.

That sounds like an insult, but I mean the exact opposite. If this is where the game is at launch, at its most barebones, running on years-old consoles on their way out, then think of what it will be like at its peak.

I work for PC Gamer, so forgive my snobbery when I say the PC version should be far superior to what we're right now playing on consoles.

A part of that is the possible frame rate bump from running on modern PC hardware. The standard PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series S/X are powered by pretty outdated architectures by today's standards: RDNA 2 and Zen 2. You're looking at the Radeon RX 6000 series and Ryzen 3000 series for PC equivalents.

These chips have recently received support for more modern ML-powered FSR upscaling techniques from AMD, though Rockstar has only seen fit to enable FSR 4 on the Xbox Series S to help the underpowered console along. Sony also has AMD-powered upscaling tech for the PS5 Pro, but the standard PS5 doesn't get a whiff of that.

It's only really the PS5 Pro with a more modern GPU—loosely equivalent to an RX 7800 XT—that might temper expectations for how fast the game may run on a modern gaming PC. Rockstar has said the PlayStation 5 Pro wouldn't be capable of a steady 60 fps even with the more powerful hardware compared to the base model; however, hints at the sluggish CPU as perhaps the weak link. The PS5 Pro runs the same old eight-core CPU as the standard PS5, and if Rockstar's engine can make use of faster, more multithreaded CPUs with lots of cache, we should see a performance bump on PC.

That's not to exclude older gaming PCs. The Xbox Series S can cope with GTA 6, so should many gaming PCs of all levels. Notably so if Rockstar offers a range of upscaling options.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It's ubiquitous upscaling that should make an even bigger difference to an eventual PC release and performance on all manner of PC. We know the game supports FSR 4.1, as both Sony and Microsoft are already using this as the foundation for their upscaling technologies on console, and Red Dead Redemption 2 offers both FSR and DLSS on PC. Since that game's release, we've seen the advent of frame generation technologies from both AMD and Nvidia, which could further increase how smooth GTA 6 feels on PC.

As a serial settings tweaker, I've been sorely disappointed by the sliders, or lack thereof, available to me in GTA 6 on the base PS5. I want levels to this stuff; an advanced menu for advanced men like me. I want to manage the foliage detail, draw distance, and ray-traced effects. Speaking of which, I'm sure we'll have the option to enable ray-traced shadows, at the moment exclusive to the PS5 Pro, and crank up the quality of most effects in the game on PC.

The non-RT shadows are one of the few noticeable drawbacks about the standard PS5 version of GTA 6 I'm at the moment playing. They can pop in and out from reflections, and there is a jagginess to them in places.

Is any game going to be modded more than GTA 6? Our Joshua has been busy modding GTA 5 to try to turn it alchemy-like into GTA 6 for months now, and he never ran out of mods to install. While he may have strayed from his original mission almost immediately, the message is clear: GTA 6 is going to have a seriously busy mod scene.

The game will be all the better for it, too. Not every mod is going to enable a roving band of militant furries (Joshua's words, and no need to mod those into GTA 6) or trap the player in a tiny car; I'm sure GTA 6 will actually be a better game for the efforts of modders. It just takes a PC version and some intrepid people to make it happen.

Recent findings suggest that this one is easy; one of the reasons for GTA 5's long-lasting legacy is the combination of GTA Online and custom jobs via the creator. Neither of which are actually here for GTA 6 yet. So on a very basic level, and you don't have to be a PC gamer to agree on this point, GTA 6 is going to get a lot better for the eventual online mode. And there will be an online mode, right? Even if Rockstar hasn't technically unveiled one is on the way yet.

On the flipside, if you're constantly getting griefed by a guy that only plays GTA 6 all day and won't let you leave your house in GTA Online, perhaps you could argue the game was better when it was single-player only.

It pains me to admit it, but GTA 6 is not only going to eventually run better on PC. It might be the definitive version in my eyes, but console gamers do have a high-fidelity future ahead of them, too. Both Sony and Microsoft are planning newly introduced consoles that seem pretty likely to come out in roughly a year's time—providing the memory crisis doesn't ruin everything—and AMD is set to be providing more powerful silicon for these systems.

Sources indicate that we're expecting to see the RDNA 5 architecture make its way into the next-gen consoles, paired with Zen 6 CPU cores of some size and description (these may be heterogeneous). That would put the consoles on a level playing field with PC components likely to launch around the same time (Zen 6 should be available on desktop by then, while perhaps a more limited launch for RDNA 5 by early 2028).

According to recent reports, so that whole spiel about how current-gen consoles are years behind our fancy PCs won't get me so far once these upcoming systems come out. I'll have to find a new stick to bash consoles with… er, not enough RGB LEDs? Anyways, the definitive GTA 6 experience on console is still yet to come—that'll be the version that's ready to make the most of these more capable units sometime next year or in 2028.

There are going to be a helluva lot of patches, upgrades, and DLCs to come for GTA 6. Remember, GTA V got a new first-person mode with the then-next-gen PS4 and Xbox One, so there's plenty of opportunity for genuine upgrades down the line.

Though, saying that, by recent PC standards (poor ports, game-breaking bugs, and more), this GTA 6 launch has been relatively issue-free. I mean, I've seen a couple of visual glitches and my colleagues have had some strange men falling out of the sky, but besides those open-world oddities you may expect of a game of this size and stature, it's been pretty smooth sailing so far.

It has been revealed that I just hope the PC version can claim a similarly clean sweep for its eventual launch. So far, no word on when that might be.

World of Warcraft: Forever's in-game economy has been ravaged by an exploit that allowed players to farm thousands of gold

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (819 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • World of Warcraft: Forever has suffered its first economic nightmare, as a dungeon farm exploit has left some players with thousands of gold in their bags while the vast majority of players are barely above their first hundred.
  • This exploit was swiftly and quietly hotfixed by Blizzard, but not before a presently-unknown number of players were able to make out like bandits.
  • This was possible on every class, and according to Twitch streamer Ziqo, allowed players to farm out hundreds of gold in a few hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever has suffered its first economic nightmare, as a dungeon farm exploit has left some players with thousands of gold in their bags while the vast majority of players are barely above their first hundred.

This exploit was swiftly and quietly hotfixed by Blizzard, but not before a presently-unknown number of players were able to make out like bandits. In basic terms, the new Blackmaw Hold dungeon includes several packs of non-elite, easy to kill enemies right at the start of the dungeon. Prior to the hotfix, the loot drop tables for these enemies were incorrect, and worth vastly more in terms of gold than they should have. Keen-eyed players spotted this but kept it quiet, running into the dungeon and quickly killing off these early mobs and resetting the dungeon every hour.

This was possible on every class, and according to Twitch streamer Ziqo, allowed players to farm out hundreds of gold in a few hours. He is seen streaming with over 4,000 gold - and claims other streamers made out with more than that.

For an idea of how much money that is, one of the most expensive things a player will likely buy on their character throughout the original Classic World of Warcraft is the expert riding skill. It takes a long time to save up for, and stands as a major accomplishment in the life of a character. It costs around 900 gold. These players, in just a few days of dedicated grinding, will have been able to pay this price several times over.

Sources indicate that looking at community hubs for the game (Reddit or the official World of Warcraft forums), regular players are demanding Blizzard take action - going further than just the already-deployed hotfix. Maya on the WoW forum wants the ill-gotten gold to be removed and for players to be banned who made use of the Blackmaw Hold exploit, writing: "Remove the gold or I and many others will just quit. This is worse than the bots at this point.".

Recent findings suggest that flnrodi on Reddit, referring to streamers who took advantage of this exploit, wrote: "Not sure what to say. The fact that he did this all offstream claims enough that [Ziqo] (and others) knew that this is not intended and 100 percent considered an exploit. Personally, I think there should be some kind of punishment and definitely all the gold [should be] revoked.".

You may be wondering why this is such a major deal? So what if a few players can get fancy mounts faster, or snatch up some really good gear on the player auction house? Well, exorbitant sums of money in the hands of a few players can have a massive impact on a server's economy. You could, for example, use your newfound wealth to flip every listing of a certain rare resource on the auction house and mark the price up significantly for profit, which obviously inflates the price for regular players. Likewise, you can out-bid other players for rare and powerful BOE items, which in turn raises the prices of those as sellers may find they can make more cash than they could off such drops prior to the exploit.

This all has an inflationary effect, and could push a server's economy to a more expensive level faster than it otherwise would. Even if this effect isn't so drastic, these players can essentially gear out multiple characters in fantastic gear without putting in the hours, or out-bid the rest of the community on the Black Market Auction House for rare and largely unparalleled special loot.

It has been revealed that the counter argument against punitive measures is that these players didn't cheat. They didn't buy gold from real-money-traders, nor did they plug in some external tool to give them an unfair advantage over others. They simply put in the time to get to around level 55, ran a dungeon, and killed mobs repeatedly for valuable drops. Would it have been a good thing to flag the exploit the moment they found out about it? Sure. But once other players at your level take advantage of it, and no strict ruling around whether doing so is punishable, it's arguably in a player's best interest to join in while the going is good.

In a recent development, as of writing, there's been no official word from Blizzard on what it intends to do beyond fixing the exploit. Given the required level to take on Blackmaw Hold, the number of exploiters cannot be too large, and the sheer amount of gold they gained in a small amount of time should make them easy to flag. Rolling back their accounts and reverting the gold they gained back to a pre-exploit amount certainly appears to be a popular option. Whether Blizzard actually does so, or enforces other punishments, is the massive question.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6's Mandy is probably someone most of you already know if you've played the game for a few hours or have been within 10 feet of the internet the past few days. I say this because such a ruckus has been kicked up that even former Nintendo of America president Reggie Fils-Aimé has taken notice. Gang, have we stayed too far from god's light?

The answer is yes, but I continue. To catch you up, some of GTA 6's early game in chapter 1 sees Jason doing the rounds to run some errands for those closest to him. Part of that involves getting rent from people who aren't paying Brian on time. One of those people is Mandy.

According to recent reports, when you go around to visit her, she states the rent will only be paid when her sink is fixed. So, being the fixer you are, you do just that. And then it gets weird. What does Jason find in Mandy's sink in GTA 6? A severed finger, of course. And what does Jason see when he looks up to ask what that's all about? Mandy in a bikini that can only be described as several sizes too small. Regardless, while her attempts to seduce Jason didn't work, it certainly did on the internet.

In a recent development, what you're supposed to do next is take a look around and see the red flags that point to Mandy clearly being some sort of serial killer. That's not what's happened for most. Most were too stun-locked to do much more than eventually eat her apples and wander off, cursing Rockstar for insisting they be faithful to Lucia.

In a recent development, I know this brief scene has had an impact on many of you – one, because I can see that the internet and trend data sent to me by our audience team have yet to neglect her name. But also, even Reggie Fils-Aimé is noticing it.

Over on the ol' global town square, former Nintendo marketing lead Krysta Yang asks if GTA 6 is "adult Animal Crossing?" I mean, kind of. You can very much play it as a life sim and do bits and bobs like fix up your house and run errands. In response, Fils-Aimé quickly emphasizes the adult part, asking, "If so, where's Mandy?".

He's certainly not the first person to ask that question this week, that's for sure.

Recent findings suggest that for all intents and purposes, Black Friday sales are already here. There are plenty of deals out already, even though we're weeks away from the actual event. One of the reasons for that is the competition retailers have with each other to be the first to get your money. One of the retailers that is making the biggest early splash is Best Buy, confirming their entire proposal for the rest of the year. Here's what you need to know.

Best Buy has revealed the following events:.

DoorBoosters: A Halloween sale from Oct. 30 to Nov. 1.

Industry observers note that early Black Friday Deals and Doorbusters: The official start of early Black Friday deals on Nov. 6. New deals will drop every Friday.

Industry observers note that black Friday Doorbusters and Deals: Best Buy says this will be its main sale, starting on Thursday, Nov. 19 and running until Nov. 28 with deals on "computing, gaming, home theater, wearables, and more.".

Cyber Sunday and Monday: Best Buy is extending Cyber Monday to five days and states you can find deals going up to 50% off select tech.

Last-minute savings: The Christmas sale will run from Dec. 18 until Dec. 24.

According to recent reports, you can find deals on TVs, laptops, headphones, video games, electric bikes, and more. There will be new deals every week in stores, on its website, and in the Best Buy mobile app. They'll offer price matching, meaning if the price drops further during the sale (Dec. 24), they will match it and offer a refund.

Here are the best deals I've found so far. I'll be updating these deals throughout the sale, so make sure to come back and see what's new. Remember that new deals drop every day.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sony has managed to squeeze out another PlayStation 5 firmware patch before the highly-anticipated release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

Recent findings suggest that sony has been rolling firmware updates out on a fairly regular basis, and like many of those updates, this latest one - version 26.07-14.23.00 - doesn't bring any very meaningful changes. Sony repeated the same "we've made some security fixes to the system software" patch-note that we've seen many times before.

And like all those firmware updates, 26.07-14.23.00 is mandatory for all PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles, assuming you want to go online or play the latest games. That, of course, includes GTA 6, which requires the console's firmware to be updated to its latest version before you can play.

According to recent reports, the enhancement should download automatically the next time you turn on your console, but you can also force the download through Settings > System > System Software > System Software Update and Settings. This is also where you can tick the option for your console to automatically download and install those updates in the future.

Although Sony hasn't directly remarked so, the high frequency of those security firmware updates is likely related to the impending release of GTA 6, especially in light of recent gen-AI-driven PS5 jailbreaks.

Any firmware released before GTA 6's release now becomes required to play the game, which delays potential security exploits, seeing as hackers would need to find vulnerabilities in that firmware in order to play. While this may never happen, Sony is at least trying to minimise the risk as much as possible.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

Ubisoft has laid off 166 people from its offices in Montreal and Quebec City, saying in a statement provided to PC Gamer that its "production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs.".

Industry observers note that founded in 1997, Ubisoft Montreal is one of the biggest game studios in the world, with roughly 4,000 employees as of 2022. Ubisoft Quebec, debuted in 2005, is somewhat smaller but still substantial: Its website states the studio has "a team of over 600 creative, passionate, and innovative talents." The cuts reportedly impact employees who could not be assigned elsewhere after their existing projects were cancelled or rescoped.

Whatever the reason, it's bleak: This is the latest round in a series of layoffs that have battered the company since it announced a major restructuring in January, which followed years of struggles including workplace misconduct scandals, persistent difficulties getting games debuted, and underperformance among massive releases. Ubisoft remarked in today's half-year financial report report that it's reduced its headcount by roughly 1,100 people over the past six months.

Ubisoft did have a significant hit earlier this year with Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, but that wasn't enough to prevent post-launch layoffs at developer Ubisoft Singapore. Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot mentioned today that "Q2 exceeded our expectations, driven by the continued success of Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and solid contributions from our broader portfolio.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Wii has turned 20 years old, and looking back on its best-selling games list offers some surprising details – especially when it comes to Zelda.

Video game industry analyst at Circana Mat Piscatella shares the top 20 best-selling Wii games in the US, and while there are some obvious inclusions, it really hammers home just how massive the casual game market was at that time. Wii Play, Wii Fit, Wii Fit Plus, Wii Sports Resort, and Just Dance 2 and 3 all take top 10 slots while the other four spots are held by Mario and Mario-adjacent games. That's also without Wii Sports, which was bundled with the Wii.

Happy 20th to the Wii! Here are the all-time top 20 best-selling Wii games in the US, ranked by unit sales (excludes bundled software). It's a wild list, and yes Wii Fit was that substantial. So was Just Dance. What an era. Source: Circana Retail Tracking Service.

Obviously, Wii Play being on top isn't too surprising given that it was the best way to get a second Wiimote at launch. In the top 10, some of these titles haven't got the biggest fanbases, but it's further proof just how much of a cultural juggernaut the Wii's casual games market was – Super Mario Galaxy being the only single-player game included in the top 10.

However, it's once you get out of the top 10 that the weirdness is really emphasized, the most notable of which being the Zelda representation. Turns out, in the US, The Legend of Zelda: Twilight Princess wasn't the best-selling game in the series on the platform. So obviously, it was Skyward Sword then? It'd make sense, a launch day title versus one of the final massive titles on a console that sold tens of millions since.

In a recent development, but no. It was Link's Crossbow Training. Skyward Sword isn't even in the top 20.

11th place on the list – over Mario Party 8, Galaxy 2, and Donkey Kong Country Returns – Link's Crossbow Training stands tall. Of course, there are a few factors, with the game launching at a far cheaper price point, and being the introduction of the Wii Zapper – people loved their Wii attachments back in the day.

Minigame collection Carnival Games holds the number 20 spot by the way.

I'm modding GTA 5 every day in a quest to either transform it into a PC version of GTA 6 or break it entirely. Come back tomorrow to find out what new horrible thing I've done to Rockstar's baby, or check out what I got up to earlier.

It is time to say goodbye to Grand Theft Auto 5. Did we not say goodbye literally yesterday, when I installed a mod named Farewell Los Santos, and there was even a video and everything, and we put Komm Susser Tod over it?

No. 53 mods ago, I told you, the reader, that my mission here was to either mod GTA 5 into a version of Grand Theft Auto 6 on PC, or break the game trying. In a recent development, in other words, everything that was on the front page of GTA 5 Mods dot com's scripts section when I loaded it up this morning. This took some doing, involving quite a lot of faffing around with OpenIV and myriad .rpf packages to get everything installed.

Would you be surprised to hear (you will not be surprised to hear) the game does not start anymore? GTA 5 has gone to that great sleep that awaits us all. Oh, don't get me wrong: it will boot to the main menu, but try to resume a game or start a upcoming one and GTA 5 will, valiantly, spend about a minute and a half with its cogs audibly grinding against another before simply dumping you back at your desktop—no fanfare, no error message, just swift death. After enduring 53 other mods without completely breaking, it rests now in the great beyond.

I can't wait to do this to GTA 6.

10 Google Privacy Hacks Everyone Should Know

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (959 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that from managing your Gmail inbox to downloading apps on your Android phone, pretty much every aspect of your digital life has a little bit of Google in it.
  • Your Gmail account doesn't just have one email address.
  • If you wish to make your emails more private, you can also link your Proton Mail account to Gmail.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that from managing your Gmail inbox to downloading apps on your Android phone, pretty much every aspect of your digital life has a little bit of Google in it. That is a lot of power in the hands of a company that makes money by selling your data to advertisers. While you can't fully escape Google's tracking without quitting a whole bunch of essential online services, you can use these privacy hacks to reduce how the company tracks you, as well as protect the information in your Google account.

Your Gmail account doesn't just have one email address. In fact, it has unlimited addresses, but you need a hack to utilize them. When you're signing up for a fresh service, you can add another word to your email address, as well as the "+" symbol, to create an alias. For example, if your email is "[email protected]," and you're signing up for an Amazon account, you can use "[email protected]" as your email address. The email will still end up in your main inbox, as if you simply used [email protected]. Not only can this trick turn one Gmail address into an unlimited number of addresses, but it also helps you identify who sold your email address to spammers, because those emails will have the alias in the "To" field.

If you wish to make your emails more private, you can also link your Proton Mail account to Gmail. This lets you send and receive emails via your Gmail address, while using Proton Mail's privacy protections such as blocking email trackers.

Google wants to show you personalized search results, which initially feels very helpful, but it also ends up trapping you in an algorithmic bubble. The best way to break out of your search bubble is to periodically use other search engines, but if you wish to stick to Google, you can disable personalized search recommendations in Google Search and the Play Store on Android. Go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized Recommendations and Play Personalization.

Google tracks your web and app activity by default, which includes your search history, voice data (if you use the speak-to-search feature), and activity from sites, apps, and devices that use Google services. However, associated information, such as your location data, is also saved to your Google profile, which you might not assume gets included in "Web & app activity." Fortunately, you can disable this tracking by going to this settings page, scrolling down to "Web & App Activity," and turning off all options in this section.

Recent findings suggest that google's Timeline feature saves your location in Google Maps to create a map of places you've visited. This is useful if you want to keep track of your recent stops; however, Google can use Timeline data to help businesses see how effective their ads were, or how likely you are to visit nearby stores. Its confirmation page confirms this: "Depending on your settings, activity saved as history in your Google Account, including ad interactions, may also be connected to Timeline data to help nearby businesses estimate the likelihood that people will visit their stores. No personal information is shared with businesses.".

Timeline isn't enabled by default, but in case you enabled it a while ago, and are no longer using it, you can turn it off by going to this settings page. Click Turn off, and delete your activity to remove Timeline data from your Google account.

You can't fully escape Google's ads or tracking, but you can disable personalized ads to stop the company from using your account data to show ads. To do this, go to this settings page, and turn off Personalized ads.

While Google claims that it isn't using your emails to train AI, the organization does offer AI features that make your emails feel more robotic than human. One of these is "Smart Reply," which offers email reply suggestions such as "Got it. See you soon." I can type that on my own, and I feel uncomfortable with Gmail analyzing the contents of my emails and replies to offer suggestions that I wouldn't use anyway. You can disable this by going to Gmail Settings > General, or by visiting this settings page. Scroll down to "Smart features," and turn off the checkbox next to it. This will disable Smart Compose, Smart Reply, suggestions for pending replies and follow-ups, spelling, grammar, and autocorrect.

Industry observers note that A physical security key is a great security upgrade. It's a physical barrier that prevents most ways to hack into your account remotely. Even if someone discovers your email ID and password, and has access to your two-factor authentication code, they won't get in without physical access to that key. You can check out Google's support page for physical security keys for more information on compatibility and setting up your security keys.

Sources indicate that if you're serious about your online privacy and security, I'd advise against keeping your primary credit card saved to your Google account. If your account is compromised or your device is stolen, you risk exposing your credit card to fraud. Instead, use a prepaid virtual card with your Google account. Sites such as Privacy.com offer single-use or merchant-locked prepaid cards, and they allow you to set spending limits too. You can use such services with your Google account to reduce the chances of losing money if your account gets hacked.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You've probably heard at least a little bit of the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack from French electronic duo, Justice: a single taken from the act's original soundtrack has been released as a standalone track, and was the accompaniment to GTA 6's launch trailer. Featuring Tame Impala, SZA, and the fantastic King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, it's clear that the duo - and Rockstar - have spared no expense on the production of music for the game.

Sources indicate that from what we've heard so far, it's all very good: synth-drenched and poppy, a perfect mix of modern electronica and nostalgic throwback - ideal for the Miami-based setting of Vice City. You ought to enjoy the music while you can, though, because it seems Justice won't be coming back to video games any time soon. If ever.

Via a new interview with French publication Rockyrama, Justice's two members - Gaspard Augé and Xavier de Rosnay - shed a little light about their work with Rockstar, and their inspiration for joining the project. "When [the offer to work with Rockstar] arrived on the table, we thought 'if there’s one video game we have to do, it's this one.' As soon as we accepted and started working [on the OST], we thought it would probably be the first and last score we’ll ever do for a video game.".

Interesting. The duo, from the clip we can see on Rockyrama's posts, don't seem to give more information about this decision - did they have a bad time working with Rockstar? Was it intense? Or is it rather down to the fact that, if you're going to work on a game, you may as well make it what is largely expected to be the biggest game of all time.

Justice, for what it's worth, consider the work they've done on GTA 6 to be "a real album" of music - it's not seen as lesser or different to the band, just because it's being released as part of a video game. "GTA 6 gave us the excuse and direction to do it. The music always had to be listenable on its own, even if each track is tailored for [a specific] scene," the band explains.

In a recent development, the band's album isn't the only music connected to the game, either. There's also a 34-song album launching for the game, composed of original songs from some of the biggest artists in the world. The album features Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson and many more. The full tracklist leaked at the weekend.

It has been revealed that GTA 6 debuts on Thursday, 19th November for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week.

Industry observers note that everything's a bit grim these days, so let's just go all in on the misery shall we? Let's start with this line from the game's Steam page we'll be talking about today: "Mondrayn is a grim JRPG with survival elements where dying doesn't mean the end of your suffering." Crikey! You're telling me the sweet release of death won't be so saccharine after all? Sounds rough, so it's a good thing Mondrayn looks so darn compelling.

The world of Mondrayn is a dead one. You start out waking up in a city, it's in a gnarly state, of course, overrun by a disease of unknown origin. Horrible monsters are roaming about the place, cults are performing nasty rituals, and you've got no memories, so all you can do is try and make any friends you can, kill the undead and get out of, all places, limbo.

Mondrayn is an RPG in the sense that it utilises turn-based combat, "intertwined with shootouts." I'm not entirely sure how that manifests, you do seem to be able to do both regular attacks and special moves, the state of characters seems to have an impact, but truthfully I don't mind not understanding because what I'm here for are the utterly, delectably rancid vibes on display.

Recent findings suggest that every single pixel in this game looks like it was dipped in a vat of grime, puss, blood and vomit, and I revel in it! The enemy portraits are crunchy and violet, they look ripped straight out of some obscure art book for a Warhammer-esque tabletop game no one has ever heard of. It looks a bit fantasy, a bit steampunk, and incredibly, incredibly grimdark. It's the kind of world I'd rather instantly top myself than spend a second longer in, so, kudos to the fictional characters in it that have no choice in the matter for managing better than me. As it stands, Mondrayn has no release date, but you can wishlist it on Steam in the meantime.

Recent findings suggest that we're less than a month out from Avengers: Doomsday, and we still don't know for sure if Deadpool and Wolverine will appear in the worlds-colliding Marvel movie. But even if the chalk-and-cheese duo doesn't show up in the latest movie, the comedy outing shows us how even in the face of universes colliding, you can still have a bit of fun.

When you break it down, Deadpool 3 and Doomsday share a lot of similarities. Both movies feature Marvel heroes at risk of their respective universes being destroyed by a upcoming threat, and the only way to combat the massive bad is to join forces with other comic book figures. Heck, a sprinkle of the original Fox-era X-Men show up in both features.

But it cannot be denied that Doomsday looks a whole lot darker than the third Deadpool entry. So, with so much impending Doom (quite literally), I just hope Doomsday has taken note from Deadpool 3, and adds some humor along the way.

It has been revealed that even before it has hit screens, it is clear that the upcoming Marvel Phase 6 movie will go to some dark places. The official synopsis hints that Doomsday will close the chapter on the MCU as we know it, saying goodbye to certain heroes to make way for new ones, reading: "Courageous teams from three universes must come together to prevent a catastrophic event… Their choices and actions in this crucial moment will lay the foundation for the future of the Multiverse." In many ways, it feels like the beginning of the end.

Welcome to Road to Doomsday, GamesRadar+'s weekly MCU rewatch series. Over 15 weeks, we'll be revisiting each Marvel movie and TV show on Disney's list of essential movies to watch ahead of Avengers: Doomsday, sharing our thoughts upon rewatching and deciphering what we can learn about the next Marvel mega-event from each entry. Why not relive some MCU highlights and watch along with us?

Industry observers note that the Doomsday cast list is so unbelievably stacked that some heroes are sure to perish earlier on, and I am fearing the worst for the original Fox-era X-Men. This would make sense, as the original X-Men, including Patrick Stewart's Charles Xavier, Ian McKellen's Magneto, and James Marsden, have never been part of the MCU. So, it seems odd to bring them back now, just as a fresh X-Men movie is in the works, set to introduce a younger group of the same mutants. Yeah, it's not looking good.

Sources indicate that but Doomsday doesn't have to be all doom and gloom. Deadpool has had his fair share of setbacks, from losing his wife to literally being tortured into the scarred-faced mutant we know today. The anti-hero's traumatic background is often forgotten due to his sense of humor. He has even more hurdles thrown his way in Deadpool & Wolverine, when the TVA threatens to destroy his own universe. But, amongst the carnage, one of the most successful R-rated movies of all time still dished out the gags, from Chris Evans' cameo as Johnny Storm to Deadpool poking fun at Kevin Feige's "no-cocaine rule.".

According to recent reports, with that in mind, there's obviously something missing from Doomsday's recipe. That is, of course, self-proclaimed 'Marvel Jesus' himself and his clawed buddy. Even though Reynolds and Jackman's Doomsday casting has not been unveiled, I have a strong feeling that a cameo is on the way. Why would Marvel Studios have included Deadpool & Wolverine in its list of essential MCU movies to watch ahead of Doomsday if not? The clues are everywhere. Whenever there is a major Doomsday announcement, Reynolds is not far behind.

Avengers: Doomsday has a chance to right the wrongs of Captain America: Brave Latest World and do Sam Wilson's Cap justice.

Recent findings suggest that during Marvel's panel at San Diego Comic-Con 2026, Reynolds crashed the event dressed in a dark denim Deadpool suit (riffing off 'Jean Grey'). But we wonder why he was there at all when he doesn't have an upcoming Marvel movie to promote. The star has been leaving breadcrumbs all year, teasing his involvement by posting the Avengers logo with an anarchy sticker over the top, and saying that Deadpool "works best on scarcity and surprise." The plot thickens as Reynolds and Jackman have screenwriting credits on Avengers: Doomsday, per the Writers Guild of America’s directory, to which Reynolds responded, "Not to brag, but I do not read.".

Could Deadpool and Wolverine's unlikely duo be just what Avengers: Doomsday needs? I think so. If anything, the 2024 movie proves that when the world is at risk of complete destruction, audiences need a goofy moment or two to keep them hanging on. Of course, Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom will be a lot harder to defeat than Cassandra Nova, but with such a huge team (plus the Merc with a Mouth and Logan possibly on standby), I'm still holding out hope for the Avengers.

Deadpool & Wolverine is available to stream now on Disney Plus, ahead of the release of Avengers: Doomsday on December 18 in the US and 16 in the UK.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.
  • For riders already using Garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a fresh layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists.
  • Riders can simply opt in once through Garmin Connect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cyclists who ride with Garmin gear can now appear as live, moving icons on the Waze driving app, and nearby drivers will receive an alert to slow down and watch for them on the road.

For riders already using Garmin devices, opting in costs nothing and adds a fresh layer of safety, particularly on roads where drivers may not expect cyclists. The feature is rolling out now, but you should be aware of its limitations.

Riders can simply opt in once through Garmin Connect. After that, sharing starts automatically when an outdoor cycling activity begins and stops when the ride ends. While a ride is underway, Waze users near the cyclist see a cyclist icon move along the road and receive a Live Cycling Alert reminding them to slow down and stay aware.

Recent findings suggest that the feature runs on LiveTrack, Garmin's existing live location-sharing tool, which lets friends and family follow a rider's real-time location, speed, course, and more. Garmin says this collaboration extends that peace of mind to motorists, giving them greater awareness of their surroundings.

Industry observers note that garmin notes its location sharing is temporary and session-based. The rider's name, identity, and route are hidden, and no personal information is shared or displayed in Waze. Drivers see only an anonymous icon and the alert.

You'll need a few things to get this feature up and running:.

A compatible Garmin Edge bike computer or Garmin watch.

A phone running Garmin Connect with a data connection.

An outdoor cycling activity (the feature doesn't apply to indoor rides).

The good news is using the feature is free: LiveTrack costs nothing on compatible Garmin bike computers and watches, and Waze is free for drivers.

This fresh feature is a great safety perk, but there are real-world caveats worth considering:.

This feature is for Waze only. Alerts reach drivers only when Waze is open on their phone. Google Maps, which has far more customers, is excluded, so a large portion of the drivers you share the road with won't see you this way.

It depends on your phone's signal. Your position travels from the Garmin to your phone, then to Garmin's servers, then to Waze, and finally to the driver's phone. On a patchy rural signal, a few seconds of lag could put the icon on the wrong side of a bend from where you actually are. A rider who leaves their phone at home or whose phone loses signal simply won't show up on a Waze map, as a ride without a data connection is invisible to Waze.

In a recent development, finally, remember to treat this safety feature as an extra perk, not a guarantee. At the end of the day, it isn't a replacement for bike lights, bright clothing, and defensive riding.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February.
  • This promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies.
  • In addition, there's an alluring character skip available too.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that final Fantasy 14 is between expansions at the moment, with Evercold preparing for release in February. So, in order to keep the game populated for the next few months, Square Enix is running a special promotion in hopes of tempting players back in.

This promotion, which began yesterday, offers players a choice between two enticing freebies. Lapsed players who haven't logged in for over six months are to be given 30 days of free game time to hop back in and catch up with the main story quest ahead of Evercold's release.

In addition, there's an alluring character skip available too. If your FF14 character is at least level 90 on one class - the current level-cap is 100 - you can skip all the way to the final part of the latest Dawntrail expansion. You still need to grind to level 100 in preparation for Evercold, but the aforementioned free month of game time should provide plenty of time to do so.

In a producer letter written to accompany this promotion, Naoki Yoshida provided insight into why this was being implemented, stating that retaining players in an MMO like FF14 was of the "utmost importance".

It has been revealed that "Encouraging players to return is no mean feat", Yoshida wrote. "People pause their adventures for all kinds of reasons, including dissatisfaction and loss of interest. Although we continually update the game to address such concerns, the fact remains that getting players to resume their journey is a difficult task indeed.

"For one, I feel that the pace of change in our lives is growing increasingly fast. Back when A Realm Reborn launched, I set policies in place based on the idea that significant changes in life usually happened in roughly three-year cycles. With that in mind, we've done our best to avoid heavy-handed attempts to secure player retention through game design, and we still maintain that philosophy even today.".

It has been revealed that yoshida went on to explain that promotions such as this are meant as a "tiny nudge". He notes that those who have retained subscriptions continuously remain "the most vital" players in the development team's eyes, and acknowledges that the process of catching up in an MMO can seem "daunting" for many.

Recent findings suggest that this problem of player retention is nothing new for MMOs, especially in the tricky time between the end of a current expansion and the beginning of a new one. MMO popularity often waxes and wanes, with a new expansion acting as an exciting call to action, with the months leading up to it often serving as a natural break-point for many. Still, monthly subs pay the bills, so keeping folks around even during these quiet months is vital.

Final Fantasy 14: Evercold is looking like an especially exciting expansion. On top of the new story and two classes being added, the game is getting an overhaul to combat, with both classic Reborn and Evolved action modes, as well as a new raid difficulty meant to bridge the gap between normal and savage tiers.

The game has certainly come a long way since its initial release back in 2010. Dawntrail proved divisive among fans too, though with Evercold there's a lot of hope that a latest overarching storyline can bring the steal back the hearts of players old and new.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Valve has issued an revision on its Steam Machine stock levels, waiting lists, and purchasing process, saying that the 512GB model has now achieved "add to cart status".
  • Unfortunately, the same can't be noted of the 2TB model, which could even see further price hikes, let alone wait lists.
  • The blog post says, "We've been able to fulfill all current reservations for the 512GB model with no waitlist remaining, and have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Valve has issued an revision on its Steam Machine stock levels, waiting lists, and purchasing process, saying that the 512GB model has now achieved "add to cart status". After months of joining a lottery-based waiting list to secure the brand's alternative to a gaming PC, you can now grab the entry-level model and its bundled controller with no waiting or reservation constraints.

Unfortunately, the same can't be noted of the 2TB model, which could even see further price hikes, let alone wait lists. Valve posted an update to its hardware blog yesterday evening, confirming that despite the doom and gloom of the 2TB model, "We've finished getting purchase invites out to all reservation holders.".

The blog post says, "We've been able to fulfill all current reservations for the 512GB model with no waitlist remaining, and have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders.

"However, we are continuing to encounter supply constraints for hardware components, which impacts our ability to source parts.".

The Steam Machine, along with the Steam Controller and Steam Frame, were all meant to launch in "early 2026", but the very same supply constraints Valve is mentioning this week caused massive delays and (presumably) substantial price hikes on the firm's upcoming generation of hardware.

On the 2TB model's future availability, Valve indicates: "We expect to have more details to share in January about additional supply.".

But given the RAM shortages that are ongoing, and that SSD prices just keep increasing, it's highly likely that Valve will need to jump the 2TB model's price to even higher ranges in the fresh year, because the current RAM and SSD situation shows no sign of stopping.

"We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units, but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them," indicates Valve.

With more updates in January, it seems as though Valve is issuing a fairly general and open-ended statement here in order to leave a lot of wiggle room. But the above quote in particular leaves the possibility open for a temporary discontinuation of the 2TB model, or a price hike on upcoming stock.

Thankfully, if people are still on the waiting list for a 2TB model, Valve is allowing them to choose a 512GB model instead while supplies last, while opting out of the queue for the 2TB version.

That may be the best alternative when stock levels are this uncertain, as Valve claims, "the number of customers on the waitlist exceeds our current production; even when we are able to build more it will be at smaller quantities than we planned.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Using cheats in GTA 6 is a given. GTA games are big, beautiful sandboxes of destruction, and sometimes I want to forget about story missions and just magically fill my pockets with cash, spawn a tank or a jet, and go on a rampage with infinite incendiary ammo.

Sources indicate that naturally, you can do that with GTA 6 cheats. But only eventually. If you were hoping to try out some cheats the moment you step into the game, I've got some bad news for you—and then some worse news. Here are the problems:.

Maybe that's fair—Rockstar devs don't want you busting out cheats and skipping through the game they spent 10 years crafting. But then again, if you shell out potentially $100 for a game, shouldn't you be able to play it however the heck you want? I think so.

GTA 6 is a major, long game, with a five chapter main story that contains 91 missions. It took me about 90 hours to finish, at which point I could finally access the cheats menu.

That's where I found the next bit of bad news...

Congrats on playing those 90 hours: are you ready for 90 more? Most cheats on the menu are locked because there are requirements you need to meet to use them. Want a cheat that removes fall damage? First you'll need to survive 20 falls of over more than 40 feet. Want to spawn a parachute? First complete 50 skydives and basejumps.

Industry observers note that using an infinite ammo cheat means first winning 25 medals on shooting ranges. To fast-forward time you'll need to find 10 collectible watches—and in 90 hours I found exactly one of them. Spawning a jet means first completing every single challenge in the game, which is gonna take, ooh, let me check… forever.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

I don't love this cheat unlock system at all, but there's even more bad news:.

Want to use a cheat to give yourself an extra $250,000 so you can go on a car buying spree? Cool, go ahead. But you won't be able to save your progress once you enable a cheat.

In a recent development, whatever fun you have cheating is purely of the sandbox variety. You can buy cars and clothes and guns with cheated money, but you'll lose it all when you stop playing because you're not allowed to save your game once you use a single cheat. Booo.

And there's one final bummer for ya:.

It has been revealed that I tried it. I opened an older save where I hadn't yet completed the main story, and tried to input the cheats I'd learned from my complete game save. No dice! The cheats don't work unless you're using a save file that's story complete. So, starting over at the beginning and using cheats? Not gonna happen.

I'm really not a fan of this. With so many restrictions in place, Rockstar has really taken the fun out of being a huge GTA cheater! When GTA 6 finally comes to PC, I hope modders make cheats their top priority.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the promise of user-generated content, this idea that you could host a platform that grows infinitely because the people that interact with it make things for it and you don't even have to pay anyone, is an alluring one. And its siren call has come for Dead by Daylight, as developer Behaviour Interactive have outlined the future of the game, which includes a way to make your own bits for the multiplayer horror game.

It has been revealed that "What if you could create your own Dead by Daylight experiences?" explains a blog post recapping the intends for how the game is going to change. "As one of the most exciting updates coming in 2027, the Dead by Daylight Workshop will open the doors to user-created content in some incredible ways. From designing your own Maps and importing custom assets, to modifying game rules, objectives, and even creating entirely latest modes, the possibilities are vast.".

The post goes on to note that anything created in the workshop will "exist separately from all our classic modes, with dedicated creation tools and moderation provided to ensure experienced modders have everything they need to do their best work, and all submissions meet our official guidelines." I am always hesitant when it comes to UGC faff, because the ability to make your own custom Debbie Daylight maps might sound promising, but people do actually have to engage with them for the whole thing to work. It's just putting a hat on a hat!

Sources indicate that anyway, the workshop isn't the only thing Behaviour have in the works. For one, the game is getting a massive visual overhaul. You can expect lighting improvements, more detailed assets and "tons of atmospheric touches," alongside revamps of particular maps like the Temple of Purgation and Backwater Swamp. Killers and survivors will be getting some TLC too by "improving character textures, proportions, hair, and animations to make them look and feel more lifelike. That includes updated character rigs, new motion capture, and new facial animation technology designed to better express a character’s fear, pain, and struggles over the course of a Trial.".

Beyond all of that, a dynamic weather system is coming to the game, meaning you'll now have to deal with the likes of rain, thunderstorms, snow and heavy wind, all of which can impact matches. Onboarding for newer folks should be getting some improvements too, with the addition of a "more cinematic introduction, clearer explanations and tutorials of game mechanics, and a more gradual introduction," to the game. All of this will be coming in one big patch sometime in 2027, so, keep your eyes peeled for whenever that drops.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that "The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," remarked Mitsuda.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chrono Trigger composer Yasunori Mitsuda thinks it may be time for Square Enix to retire Dragon Quest, while reflecting on the direction of the popular RPG series after Akira Toriyama's death. The mangaka, whose art and distinct style were foundational to Chrono Trigger and Chrono Cross - and are still used in Dragon Quest to this day - died in 2024 at the age of 68.

Today, speaking via a blog post on his personal website (hat tip, Power Up Gaming), Mitsuda - a colleague of Toriyama's back in the SNES/Chrono Trigger days - suggested that maybe it's time to retire the franchise in favour of something latest. This was all triggered by the announcement of Dragon Quest RPG: The Island of the Demon Tree and the Guided Island, an iOS and Android game that uses art that is very reminiscent of Toriyama's.

Industry observers note that "The Toriyama-style illustrations for [Dragon Quest RPG] have become a hot topic, but I feel that this direction is not good for the artist, Toriyama Akira fans, and even for the late Toriyama Akira himself," remarked Mitsuda. "As a personal opinion, since it's impossible to create anything truly new no matter how hard you try, I feel that the Dragon Quest series should be brought to an end for now, and [Dragon Quest creator, Yuji Horii] should create a new RPG. (There have been many remakes already.)".

Horii himself seems undeterred: with the new mobile game's announcement last week, he noted that the goal of his new project is to "capture that unmistakable Dragon Quest feeling" that comes with "exploring towns, meeting new allies, gearing up and steadily growing stronger". As Mitsuda calls for the series to retire, and for something new to take its place, Horii is keen to bring "the same classic adventure" to your smartphone.

"What's crucial is that the game provides dreams, hope, and experiences that can only be had through games to the younger generation of children who will play it in the future," concluded Mitsuda. "But every time I see topics like this, I realise just how wonderful Dragon Quest is and how it has captivated so many people.".

It's unlikely Square Enix is going to want to drop the series, of course: the Dragon Quest 3 HD-2D Remake exceeded Square Enix's (in)famously lofty expectations, and as the company aggressively pursues its multiplatform strategy, it's hard to imagine a world in which it's going to want to move away from a series that routinely pulls in millions of sales.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Years after we noted goodbye to Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark, they return for another surprise appearance in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.

Once again, Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson return as the District 12 victors – and they're not alone, either, with Woody Harrelson also returning as Haymitch Abernathy.

Industry observers note that "The energy was great. It was great to have the three of them back," Francis Lawrence, who has directed five out of six Hunger Games movies, tells us when we meet with him in London to discuss the film. "I've done four movies with Jen, and so we remain in touch as with Josh and Woody, and they stay in touch, and so it's not like we haven't seen each other in years and years and years or anything.

"But I think to reunite as a whole for the purpose of making something that's Hunger Games related was really special," he continues. "We're a bit of a family, everybody that makes these movies, and that's crew included. And so, when Jen and Josh and Woody all came in, they landed in Germany, and I remember getting a text from Jen that she and Josh were in the bar having a beer, and I was wrapping. And so, I came in, and Nina [Jacobson, producer] came in, and the DP came in, and this camera operator came in, and our sound guy, and our stills guy, and suddenly there's 40 people who have been making these movies together for years, and that reunion I think was really the special part. A shoot day is a shoot day, and it was nice to do, but I think just having everybody in that whole family that's been there – at least with me since 2012 – together, having a drink before the shoot was really fun.".

Sunrise on the Reaping also introduces some newcomers to the franchise, including McKenna Grace as District 12 tribute Maysilee Donner, Joseph Zada as a younger version of Haymitch, and Whitney Peak as Haymitch's Covey girlfriend Lenore Dove Baird.

In a recent development, "I was so giddy. I was really giddy," Peak says of her reaction to the return of Lawrence, Hutcherson, and Harrelson.

It has been revealed that though the return was confirmed by Lawrence before the film was released, there was an attempt at keeping the trio's presence secret on set. "They all had fake names on the call sheet as well," indicates Zada, with Grace adding: "It was completely fake names, and we were all like, 'Who are the blank faces on the call sheet?' Like, come on!" Says Peak: "Top of the call sheet as well, like, 'Yeah, we know who this is!'".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

videogame executive Peter Moore, known for his time at Sega, Xbox, and Electronic Arts as well as a couple of famous tattoos, has expressed hope that the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 will provide a much-needed "shot in the arm" for the videogame industry.

Moore began with a faked photo of himself rolling up his sleeve to reveal a GTA 6 tattoo—although the photo is based on his real-world tattoo-based reveal of Grand Theft Auto 4 on Xbox 360 at E3 2006.

"In all seriousness, the videogame industry could really use a moment like this," Moore wrote on X after posting the image. "We've been through a challenging period. Studio closures, redundancies, cancelled projects and enormous uncertainty have taken their toll on an industry that has given so much to so many, myself included.

"That's why the launch of GTA 6 feels so significant. It's more than the release of a hugely anticipated game. It's an opportunity to remind the world of the extraordinary power of this industry to create, innovate, entertain and bring people together.".

Moore's career in the game industry began at Sega, where he oversaw the launch of the Dreamcast and promptly rose to become president and chief operating officer of Sega of America. In 2003 he went to Microsoft and became its Corporate Vice President of Interactive Entertainment Business, Entertainment and Devices Division, heading up its Xbox division; in 2007 he joined EA Sports, and eventually became the company's chief operating officer. He left the videogame business behind in 2017 to head up Liverpool FC, but it did not work out: Despite a highly successful run, club ownership did not care for his very public style of leadership, and in 2020 his contract was not renewed.

And he did indeed announce GTA 4 with a tattoo—apologies for the resolution, it was 20 years ago.

In today's message, Moore stated he's "seen this industry reinvent itself time and time again" over those years, and expressed hope that GTA 6 delivers not just commercial success but also "a much-needed shot in the arm (no pun intended…) for the entire ecosystem: developers, publishers, studios, retailers, technology partners and the next generation of creative talent.".

"The games industry has always been at its best when it dares to dream major," Moore concluded.

In a recent development, moore's upbeat sentiment stands in sharp contrast to that expressed yesterday by game industry legend Warren Spector, who congratulated Rockstar on the launch but stated he hopes "GTA 6 is the last of its kind" because it's such an unsustainable draw on resources: "Its billion-dollar development cost and an undoubtedly crazy marketing budget don't represent a business model anyone else can or probably should emulate. That's especially true when thousands of developers are out of work. A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries.".

I don't want to write about video games any more, I want to deliver milk in the countryside and hang out with a cow and quirky people! Sorry, what, there's a game all about that called Milki Delivery that came out today? Alright, I'll write about video games again, especially when they look as charming as this one does.

The stakes at play in Milki Delivery are very low (as are the steaks, no butchery to be found here, only one very sweet looking cow I couldn't possibly slaughter). You play as Neha, and she's made a promise to her pet cow, the titular Milki, that you'll find her a friend (I think this is a world where there aren't any cows left; yikes!). To do that, all you have to do is deliver her milk! Accept because this is an adventure game, you'll have to help out a few folks along the way.

Industry observers note that it's a game very much about the journey, as when riding about this lush and bright countryside, you might find a group of cats that just need a little taste of that sweet creamy juice you've got. Or maybe you have some rope that a farmer needs to wrassle up some sheep. Sometimes you'll have to get a bit more involved with the various people you meet, but predominantly, you'll be delivering milk to folks who need it.

Sources indicate that getting around the place is quite simple too, you plot out your path ahead of time and let the game take you as it's all mouse driven. A relaxed experience to be sure, but the game's art is just so delightful to look at, I'm quite enticed by the idea of just slowing down and enjoying some pretty pictures and making friends along the way. You can make different kinds of milk, too, just be feeding Milki different ingredients. Not how that works in real life, but now I kind of wish it was.

In any case, Milki Delivery is out now, and you can pick it up on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last Monday morning was an exciting time for fans of British spy thrillers. First, Slow Horses was renewed for Seasons 9 and 10, meaning we’ll be getting at least four more seasons of the hit show, available with an Apple TV subscription. Then, just hours later, Amazon MGM finally dropped the bomb we've all been waiting for and unveiled that the next actor to play James Bond would be Robert Pattinson. Many of us had been waiting for that for months. Years, even, yet it still came as a surprise, given the latest rumors. In hindsight, I probably should have been clued in that the announcement was imminent after the Slow Horses news dropped.

In a recent development, over the last few weeks and months, there have been a ton of rumors regarding the next Bond ahead of the long-awaited Bond 26 finally beginning production (we’re still not sure when that will actually happen). Names like Jacob Elordi, Henry Cavill, Callum Turner, and more have been rumored. Slow Horses star Jack Lowden was also heavily rumored in recent weeks. Lowden, who plays River Cartwright on the show about disgraced MI5 agents, was looking to make the jump to MI6 and become the ninth man to play Bond.

It has been revealed that it’s certainly possible for an actor to appear in multiple projects, but given Slow Horses' aggressive filming schedule (they have already wrapped Season 7, due next year, and are filming Season 8), it might have been a tough schedule to work out for Lowden had he been named Bond. When the next two seasons were declared, it should have clued me in that Lowden likely wasn’t going to be James Bond going forward. It’s quite possible that Apple may have actually been waiting on the Bond decision to announce it was moving forward with more seasons of Slow Horses, too. So, when the news dropped about the show's renewal, I should have known Bond’s announcement was on deck.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, despite the announcements coming almost at the same time, there are also rumors that Lowden might not be part of Seasons 9 and 10. A report in Variety calls Lowden’s return “uncertain.” I’m not sure what to make of that. The book-to-screen adaptation has been adapting one book per season, generally. Season 6 was an exception, as it combined two books, the 6th and 7th in Mick Herron’s series Slough House. That's not all, though.

According to recent reports, warning! There are some spoilers ahead from the books Slow Horses is adapted from!

That would presumably mean that Season 7 will be an adaptation of book #8, Bad Actors. As fans of the TV show know, Season 6 ended on a cliffhanger with River having been poisoned by the Russian assassins. Book readers know that River spends Bad Actors on the sidelines, recovering from the assassination attempt, and doesn’t appear in the novel at all. If the show has adapted Bad Actors for Season 7, might Lowden be mostly absent? Cartwright does return in the ninth book, Clown Town, which we do know is going to be Season 8 of the show.

Here’s where it gets interesting. As of today, Clown Town is the most recent book to be published in the Slough House series, so we don’t know what Herron or the producers intend to take the series, so all eyes are on Lowden!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that as much as Call of Duty is criticised for delivering the same thing every year, reports occasionally surface of attempts to take the series in bold upcoming directions, even if none of these experiments have so far seen the light of day. And it turns out a medieval Call of Duty was also explored at one time.

Sources indicate that this latest revelation comes from Infinity Ward veteran Taylor Kurosaki, who led development on the studio's Infinite Warfare and 2019 Modern Warfare game. "Call of Duty is a massive tree with a lot of branches, right?" Kurosaki told PC Gamer. "It can be World War 2. The team at IW had prototyped a medieval Call of Duty. Where you were a knight and had a sword and all kinds of crazy shit. But if it's a war story, sure, it can be Call of Duty.".

Industry observers note that this isn't the first time we've heard of an unusual Call of Duty prototype. When Activision brought Sledgehammer Games into the fold as another lead studio for the lucrative shooter series, the team briefly worked on a third-person horror off-shoot set in Vietnam, which was referred to as Fog of War.

Activision's legal battle with Infinity Ward founders Vince Zampella and Jason West, however, caused the project to be cancelled, as Sledgehammer was roped into helping the studio finish Modern Warfare 3.

In a recent development, as for Kurosaki, he currently leads That's No Moon alongside creative partner Jacob Minkoff and other Infinity Ward and Naughty Dog veterans. The studio is currently working on Crossfire, a narrative-driven third-person shooter set in the universe of Smilegate's free-to-play series of the same name.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The streaming and video creation world is all about GTA 6 right now, and that means the race is on for record-setting and benchmarking. What appears to be the first speedrun is already on the board, though I wouldn't expect the time set to hold for too long.

Less than two full days into the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, streamer BrycexD managed to hit credits through one continuous play-through, thus getting the inaugural speedrun. His time? 39:38:22.03.

Sources indicate that "I'm the very first person in the world to beat the official release version of Grand Theft Auto 6!" he writes in a tweet. "I also now hold the speedrun world record as I stayed up for 50-plus hours and took no breaks.".

It has been revealed that WE DID IT!!! I'm the very first person in the world to beat the official release version of Grand Theft Auto 6! I also now hold the speedrun world record as I stayed up for 50+ hours and took no breaks. -14,000 Combined CCV Peak -6,126 Subs - 12.2K Total -DCTY Verifier https://t.co/6fJDZJxhyeNovember 20, 2026.

That is dedication to the cause, I must say. It's hard to verify either of these claims, because we're still so close to launch and it's such a monumental release. Someone could've beaten GTA 6 already, but didn't record it, and it's entirely possible someone sped through the main narrative faster as well.

According to recent reports, speedrun.com's leaderboards don't open for another 41-and-a-half days, leaving the field open without oversight. BrycexD is certainly the most prominent and publicly visible to have achieved credits on the monolithic game, though I'm not sure his methods were advisable.

50 hours without sleep isn't healthy, and I'm not sure how enjoyable it is to plug straight into such a gargantuan latest game and time yourself getting through it. I'm glad he feels a sense of accomplishment, mind, and I can only imagine how good the sleep was afterward.

It has been revealed that the reactions are mixed in his replies. "Congrats man – but that sounds fucking horrendous in no way enjoyable," says one. "That's really crazy, man! Congrats," says another. Now we'll see who follows him, and just how much time they manage to lob off the record.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Queen's Domain's melee combat isn't for everyone: Luckily there's an in-game cheat book you can use to get a gun (and it doesn't bork your achievements cheevos or nothin').

First person King's Field/Metroid Prime-like Queen's Domain has swiftly become a top-two shortlister for my personal game of the year, but it can be a prickly, difficult-to-recommend game, particularly in its first 30 minutes or so before you get the game-defining Endu airdash sword.

I'm of a mind with news writer Josh Wolens that the contrast between pre- and post-Endu gameplay really helps sell the game's power curve, but our coworkers Andy Chalk and Morgan Park both bounced off Queen's Domain's admittedly sluggish melee combat.

There isn't a difficulty selection in Queen's Domain, but there is something close to it: A "witch's grimoire" where you can input codes to receive unique items. Most of these are references to streamers, content creators, or other indie developers.

While referential, they mesh surprisingly well with Queen's Domain's aesthetic, and I don't think they threaten its overall very deliberate sense of progression. What's more, I say playing the game at all is better than avoiding this little cheat code book out of principle.

Recent findings suggest that you can enter the code "hempie" (a reference to the vtuber of the same name) to receive a Soviet SVT-40 semi-automatic battle rifle. A bit incongruous for the medieval fantasy setting, perhaps, but I think it makes for an early game boon while not completely upending Queen's Domain's balance. Most of my preferred later game weapons have been ranged options⁠—the code just gets you one much earlier than you could otherwise. The hempie rifle has already proven an early favorite for Queen's Domain speedrunners like current world record holder Wilbun84, whose video also demonstrates where to find the grimoire.

On the starting beach, you'll notice a dead tree to your right while facing inland. There is a secret compartment on the other side of the tree, facing away from you: Press the "use" button while close to the tree to reveal the secret compartment (similar to the secret doors scattered throughout Queen's Domain). If you'd like to get even crazier with the grimoire, Destructoid has a full list of all the codes you can input with their corresponding rewards. The grimoire has a limited number of uses, so you can't get everything right away, but you can unlock more uses as the game goes on.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's board have indicated that they aren't about to do a big u-turn and reappoint recently resigned CEO Jensen Huang, following his departure after multiple alleged instances of extramarital cavorting were reported by the press. Since his exit last week, Huang has indicated he'd be open to making such a return, were it deemed best for both the tech giant and AMERICA.

It has been revealed that "On November 12th, our board of directors revealed that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as president, CEO, and board member," Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones stated during an investors call on November 17th (thanks, Percieving Calls Gamer). "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.".

That last bit seems likely to have been remarked with the intention of quieting down some of the speculation around a Huang return that's been bubbling away since he removed his bum from the black and green throne and that the exec embraced in a statement put out yesterday. "I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life," he wrote. "I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the board’s independent investigation.

Sources indicate that "Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. Nvidia is a once-in-a-generation company. If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honoured to answer these calls and return as CEO.".

For now at least, it seems leather jacketed GPUperman will not be triumphantly flying back into his former post amid a wave of corporate and patriotic fervour. Likely as part of continued efforts to reassure moneyfolk that they won't be making negative headlines again soon following Huang's departure, Nvidia's board confirmed yesterday that they're establishing a "newly introduced standing committee responsible for board-level oversight of the company’s national security policies, export control compliance and global trade risk management". One of Huang's alleged affairs was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. The Chinese government have denied the accusations of espionage.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is currently serving as Nvidia's interim CEO while the tech giant's board searches for a permanent sexy leather jacket man replacement.
