📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the very popular and critically-acclaimed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has set another record. After selling 5.2m copies in four days and becoming the Switch 2's fastest-selling game, Ocarina of Time has now been revealed to also be a major seller at retail.

Sources indicate that the remake has sold more than 1m physical copies in the US alone in its launch week (ending 7th November). That's according to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, who revealed on Bluesky that the record also makes it the first title to surpass 1m physical sales since 2023's Tears of the Kingdom. That is, no other game - from any publisher - has managed to sell over 1m copies in the US within its first week in three years.

Recent findings suggest that while Nintendo games tend to perform better at retail than those from Sony, Xbox or third-party publishers, physical sales in general have been declining in the US. In July, Piscatella revealed that just seven PlayStation games have sold more than 100,000 physical copies up to that point in 2026, and that was after all the backlash to Sony's decision to end physical disc manufacturing by January 2028.

Recent findings suggest that ocarina of Time's lead of this particular segment likely won't continue, however. That's because, as Piscatella pointed out in a follow-up post, Circana's tracking considers disc-less, code-in-box versions to be physical editions. This means Grand Theft Auto 6 will likely overtake the remake in short order, just as it's expected to break records elsewhere.

In Eurogamer's glowing review of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Christian Donlan argued that Nintendo has done just enough to modernise a timeless classic while maintaining what made the original so special for many players.

10 Movies Like ‘Interstellar’ You Should Watch Next

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: big sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing.
  • If you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you.
  • If you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, christopher Nolan’s 2014 megahit Interstellar has it all: big sci-fi ideas, cool robots, ugly crying, and a Matt Damon character in need of rescuing. Grounded in the intensity of the human experience, this story of humanity’s potential extinction and the sacrifice of one man to save it doesn’t just deliver exotic planets and thrilling spaceship maneuvers; it also provides all the feels as Joseph Cooper (Matthew McConaughey) sacrifices everything he has in an effort to save the entire human race. It’s one of the best science fiction films ever made, with Nolan’s signature complexity, time manipulations, and emotional wallop. If you love this movie, here are ten more that offer a similar viewing experience.

If you loved both the special effects in Interstellar that make space travel feel viscerally thrilling (and terrifying) and the mind-blowing concepts, this is the film for you. Stanley Kubrick’s 1968 epic (written by sci-fi master Arthur C. Clarke) traces humanity’s development from mildly smart apes to spacefaring capitalists who discover a mysterious obelisk on the Moon that sparks a mission to Jupiter. While it operates in a colder emotional key than Nolan’s film, 2001: A Space Odyssey absolutely delivers on the epic side of things (and the cool—if slightly deranged and deadly—artificial intelligences). Stream 2001: A Space Odyssey on HBO Max or rent it on Prime Video.

If you’re looking for more existential missions with somewhat reluctant heroes in space, Project Hail Mary is your next stop. When the Sun begins to dim due to the interference of an alien entity, scientists identify the one nearby star that isn’t being similarly affected. Brilliant molecular biologist Ryland Grace (Ryan Gosling) winds up forced to go on what is assumed to be a fatal, one-way mission into deep space to try to find a way to save humanity, unexpectedly assisted by a charming alien he names Rocky. It’s got the same emotional volume and big ideas as Interstellar, and fans of Nolan’s film will love it. Stream Project Hail Mary on MGM+ or Philo, or rent it on Prime Video.

Part of what makes Interstellar so compelling is the stakes: The human race is slowly dying, and a handful of people must make incredible sacrifices to save it. That’s the vibe of Sunshine, set in a future where the Sun is dimming and a spacecraft is dispatched to deliver an enormous bomb designed to reignite the Sun’s fusion cycle. But the mission is the second attempt after the first ship vanished mysteriously seven years earlier, and when the latest crew stumbles on the derelict wreck of the first mission, things rapidly descend into violence and madness—but the crew remains determined to save the world, no matter the cost. Rent Sunshine on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, interstellar works in large part because of the emotional dynamics at play. McConaughey’s character leaves his children behind and is forced to witness them growing up without him, missing out on their lives and saddled with the knowledge that they resent him despite the necessity of his mission. Arrival is a First Contact story focused on language—linguist Louise Banks (Amy Adams) is drafted into an effort to understand the strange, complex language of the aliens. As she slowly builds to an understanding of how the aliens communicate and perceive time itself, her own heartbreak and loss come into play, giving this film a similarly devastating emotional punch. Stream Arrival on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that family dynamics and the toll of lonely space missions fuel Ad Astra, a film with the same emotional core as Interstellar. Twenty-nine years ago, famed astronaut Clifford McBride (Tommy Lee Jones) led the Lima Project, a space station around Neptune searching for intelligent life. Thirteen years ago, Earth lost contact with him. When bursts of energy emanating from Neptune threaten to end life on Earth, his son, Roy (Brad Pitt), is dispatched to try to make contact with his father. It’s an epic journey with a powerful climax that will satisfy fans of Interstellar in every way. Stream Ad Astra on Netflix or rent it on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that ridley Scott’s prequel to Alien has its flaws, but if you’re looking for a sense of epic spacefaring adventure in the same key as Interstellar, it’s perfect. When two scientists discover a star map apparently left behind by ancient aliens, they secure funding from the Wayland Corporation to organize a space expedition to the indicated planet. Accompanied by a colorful crew and the android David, they discover an apparently abandoned outpost of the species dubbed the Engineers. The story wrestles with questions about humanity’s origins, purpose, and potential—but this being an Alien film, things quickly turn horrifying. Rent Prometheus on Prime Video.

Adapted from Carl Sagan’s 1985 novel, Contact follows astronomer Dr. Ellie Arroway (Jodie Foster), who becomes involved with an effort to decipher a signal originating from the star Vega. The signal turns out to be a set of instructions for constructing a one-person spacecraft of some kind, and Arroway is eventually selected as the candidate to take the journey. There’s a sense of courage in the face of the unknown that’s similar to Interstellar, as well as the thrill of strapping into a spaceship and pressing the ignition. Plus, there’s the added bonus of seeing one of the greatest trick shots in cinematic history. Rent Contact on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, stanislaw Lem’s 1961 novel Solaris explores what Lem saw as the impossibility of ever understanding a truly alien life. The two major adaptations—Andrei Tarkovsky's 1972 version and Steven Soderbergh’s 2002 take starring George Clooney—are both worth watching, but Tarkovsky’s film is a masterpiece of psychological horror. The story is set mainly aboard a space station orbiting a planet covered in what appears to be a sentient "ocean" and chronicles the strange haunting and inexplicable experiences of the humans living on the station. If your favorite part of Interstellar is the ending when things get trippy and weird, you’ll probably love Solaris. Stream Solaris on HBO Max, Plex, or Tubi, or rent it on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, the story of a mission to Jupiter’s moon Europa to search for intelligent life, Europa Report has the same sense of terrifying excitement that accompanies Interstellar’s missions to the different candidate planets. Leaning into the fragility of life in an environment not designed to support it, the mission crew face a steady stream of loss and danger as they work to catch sight of alien life on the frozen, deadly moon, ultimately faced with making terrifying sacrifices in order to provide humanity with the answers that it seeks. Stream Europa Report on Netflix, Kanopy, or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

According to recent reports, A film based on a 1956 epic science fiction poem written by a Swedish Nobel Laureate might seem like an unlikely match for fans of Interstellar, but it’s actually perfect. As the Earth becomes uninhabitable, humanity begins launching ships to colonize Mars. When one such ship, the Aniara, is damaged and veers irreversibly off course, the passengers and crew are faced with the knowledge that they will sail off into the void without hope of rescue. Within a few years, despair has driven some to suicide and madness, while others cling to the possibility that they might yet find a way back. The film offers a different perspective on the existential crisis of humanity’s extinction, exploring the worst-case scenario to its bitter, bleak end. Stream Aniara on Kanopy or Hoopla, or rent it on Prime Video.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.
  • If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep.
  • According to recent reports, is the nickname FemJun too blatant?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sci-fi role-playing game Exodus continues to play into the Mass Effect comparisons by revealing the female version of its main character Jun, and with studio Archetype referring to her in marketing material as FemJun.

If that moniker sounds familiar it's because it is: the female Commander Shepard character in the Mass Effect series was nicknamed FemShep. FemShep became an iconic part of BioWare's iconic series, eventually proving that female leads could front games just as successfully as male leads could, and be every bit as popular.

According to recent reports, is the nickname FemJun too blatant? Possibly. But there's well publicised BioWare pedigree at Archetype Entertainment, in the studio's co-founders and in the people leading the project. Key Mass Effect writer Drew Karpyshyn is in charge of writing Exodus, for example, and the similarities to Mass Effect are something the Exodus team has not been shy about in the past. In the wake of Mass Effect 5 being cancelled and BioWare being closed, they become even more alluring.

Recent findings suggest that there are, however, massive and crucial differences between Exodus and Mass Effect, key among them, time dilation. In Exodus, there are special Exodus missions whereby you leave your home planet and fly far away, and in doing so experience time differently to the people back home. Many years will pass for them while only days will pass for you, which provides the game with a way to show you long-term consequences of your actions when you return.

Recent findings suggest that archetype hasn't shown the female version of Jun before, despite having released many videos of Exodus, perhaps to build anticipation for her reveal. It's a press beat that's also provided Archetype - a studio owned by Dungeons & Dragons company Wizards of the Coast - with an occasion to reveal the two actors playing Jun in the game.

Female Jun is portrayed by Carina Conti, who played the lead in the recent Mafia game, The Old Country - Isabella Torrisi. She's appeared in HBO's Winning Time and Hulu/Freeform's Good Trouble as well. Male Jun, meanwhile, is portrayed by Stephen Oyoung, who played Mister Negative in Insomniac's Marvel's Spider-Man 1 and 2 games, and Red Hood in Gotham Knights. He also appeared in Mission: Impossible - The Final Reckoning, The Wrecking Crew, and Twisters. The game also famously stars Matthew McConaughey.

Archetype declared a Dark Horse hardback art book to go on sale alongside the game next year as well. This arrives a week after the game; Exodus arrives 7th April 2027 on PC, PS5 and Xbox Series S/X, and the art book on 13th April.

It has been revealed that matt played Exodus at Gamescom relatively recently and came away impressed, referring to it as "the best kind of surprise". "I wasn't expecting quite such a bombastic 45 minutes when I first picked up a controller and settled into Exodus, admittedly, but the more I played, the more it made sense," he wrote. "I might not be much of a Mass Effect fan (damn you M35 Mako once more), but Exodus is now firmly on my radar ahead of its arrival next year.".

This new adventure takes place one year after the events of Professor Layton and the Unwound Future.

The story unfolds in America, where the Wild West era has ended and the country is forging ahead into a new age of development.

A letter from Luke leads Layton to Steam Bison, a town renowned for its inventions….

Steam Bison has undergone rapid technological advances thanks to the steam engine. But mysterious events are unfolding one after another, from a phantom gunman who has kidnapped a wealthy heiress to a gang of zombies threatening the town. Layton and Luke join forces once again to investigate these strange occurrences and embark on a grand puzzle-solving adventure.

◆ A Story That Unfolds as You Solve Puzzles.

You’ll encounter all kinds of puzzles as you explore the streets of Steam Bison.

—Even to meet Eggmuffin, an inventor, you’ll need to solve a puzzle to find the entrance to his room….

—Solve the puzzle, and the story moves forward.

◆ The Most Puzzles in Series History.

Layton and Luke face more puzzles than ever before in the series. Solve a wide variety of puzzles as you progress through the story and get to the bottom of the mysterious events unfolding in Steam Bison. Along the way, you’ll even come across puzzles that play a part in Steam Bison’s development. Solve them to upgrade the town’s facilities and watch the town flourish.

—Solve puzzles to develop facilities!

What’s more, a newly introduced puzzle will be added to Daily Puzzles every day for over a year following launch. This lets you enjoy the game long after you’ve completed the story.

Whether you prefer to take your time solving puzzles on your own or gather around a major screen with family and friends to work them out together, that’s all part of the fun of the Layton series.

The duck robot that monitors the factory won’t stop once it’s set in motion! Give it the right commands to overcome obstacles and complete the operational test.

Experience Professor Layton and the New World of Steam in different languages! Choose your preferred languages for text and voice, and set off on an adventure with Professor Layton and Luke! Mix and match languages to experience the story in a whole new way!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that freshly published bankruptcy documents for perennially troubled MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy have spelled out the scale of the company's debt, with around £61.7 million owed to creditors. The documents also touch on founder Leslie Benzies and CEO Mark Gerhard's claims that MindsEye is the victim of an organised sabotage campaign. The company's leaders have apparently taken out even more loans in order to fund legal action against the suspected perpetrators, with the promise of a healthy payout. I'm not holding my breath.

Industry observers note that BARB's largest debt by far is the roughly £36.5 million owed to NetEase, publishers of Marvel Rivals. Asset manager Diameter Capital Partners are the second largest external creditor, having loaned BARB around £4.25 million. A further $19 million is owed to "group undertakings" – "group undertakings" meaning debts to parent companies, subsidiaries or fellow subsidiaries. Studio founder Benzies, meanwhile, is owed £1,158,167.05. Given that Benzies has been repeatedly accused of torpedoing MindsEye's fortunes by way of disruptive micro-management, I'm not sure many BARB staff would agree that he really deserves his million quid back at this stage, but that's what it claims on paper. Smaller IOUs include £10,434.11 for Amazon Web Services, £634.36 for Unity, and a mighty £19.90 for OpenAI.

Industry observers note that build a Rocket Boy have been on a journey, it's fair to say. Announced in 2023, their flagship project MindsEye is a filmic GTA-ish action shooter initially billed as a full-fat demo for Everywhere, a game creation platform comparable to Roblox. MindsEye struggled to compel us before launch and did not find its people on release, with poor sales leading to layoffs even as BARB leadership insisted they could revive the game's fortunes.

Sources indicate that the same leadership were subsequently accused by their own staff of "disastrously" mishandling the redundancies and enforcing "unbearable" crunch. Unionised BARB employees have now taken management to court for installing alleged surveillance software on their work PCs. The game's publishers Io Interactive noped out of the picture in March this year. Meanwhile, Benzies and Gerhard have thrown around accusations of a sinister espionage and sabotage campaign, carried out by unspecified perpetrators. They made a sort of revenge fantasy DLC pack about it, which our own Mark Warren characterised as we-already-have-Hitman-at-home. The bankruptcy documents shed more light on these twists and turns. According to the administrators, BARB were "funded mainly by equity investment from institutional, strategic and venture capital investors over several funding rounds, including a $110m Series D round in 2023." This followed a £32 million investment in 2020, as reported by GI. The organization grew significantly during MindsEye's creation to around 500 UK and overseas employees. According to a group income statement, the company posted sequential operating losses of £47.5 million for the period ending September 30th, 2025, and £63.1 million for the year ending December 2024. The administrator proposals document also devotes some time to the aforesaid allegations of sabotage. "The directors formed the view that the game's commercial prospects may have been adversely affected by a coordinated campaign of negative online reviews and commentary," it reads. "The directors subsequently received information which they considered suggested the involvement of a number of third parties in organising and funding such activity and commenced litigation against some of those parties. The directors have indicated that such claims may be substantial in value, although the extent of any recovery remains uncertain and will be dependent upon the outcome of ongoing investigations, legal proceedings and asset recovery actions." A later section vaguely alludes to the sum BARB leadership hope to recover. "Prior to the Joint Administrators' appointment, the Company had undertaken detailed investigations and had commenced litigation against several third parties, with the assistance of the Company's former legal advisers, Brandsmiths, in connection with matters described earlier in the Proposals," the doc reads. "The Joint Administrators consider the litigation potentially to be the largest asset of the Administration." The document goes on that BARB management have "sought financial support from third party investors to fund the anticipated legal costs and expenses associated with the litigation", with some of these funding agreements already executed. "Further executed agreements and associated funding contributions are expected to be received, shortly, and a substantial litigation fund is anticipated to arise," it continues. The Joint Administrators are "presently engaging in the on-going litigation, progressing the funding arrangements entered into by the Company, and have assessed the merits of pursuing the litigation". They will liaise with relevant parties to "determine the most appropriate strategy for preserving and, where appropriate, realising value from this potential asset for the benefit of creditors and other stakeholders." The doc doesn't name who, exactly, is being taken to court. As far as I'm aware, it isn't us. Anyway, it's good to know that the company who owe over £60 million are taking on more debt in order to pursue a histrionic grievance for which they have yet to supply any real evidence whatsoever.

Your GTA 6 car is your Red Dead 2 horse, and it's perfect

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (805 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Pcgamer

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every time the very concept of a GTA 6 has come up in the past eight years, I've had just one wistful opinion to contribute: "I hope they make it more like Red Dead Redemption 2.".
  • Recent findings suggest that I'm not a huge GTA guy, but I am a Red Dead head.
  • There was no way Rockstar would repeat all of these life sim-y touches for the louder and faster GTA 6, but I am surprised and elated that my favorite Red Dead 2 feature of them all made the cut: Your car is your horse.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every time the very concept of a GTA 6 has come up in the past eight years, I've had just one wistful opinion to contribute: "I hope they make it more like Red Dead Redemption 2.".

Recent findings suggest that I'm not a huge GTA guy, but I am a Red Dead head. The sequel is Rockstar's best work (maybe second best now?) because of all the ways it prioritizes roleplay and choice-making by simulating the little things: Mixing tonics, crafting bullets individually, grooming Arthur's mustache. God, I love that stuff.

There was no way Rockstar would repeat all of these life sim-y touches for the louder and faster GTA 6, but I am surprised and elated that my favorite Red Dead 2 feature of them all made the cut: Your car is your horse.

Industry observers note that that is to say, Jason and Lucia's personal vehicles are their mobile bases—an essential extension of them. You can't pet or name it, sadly, but it's vital to keep track of and take care of your whip, because it's where you keep all your guns and outfits. It's all literally in the trunk: If you want to fetch your shotgun, you have to walk to the back of the car, open it up, and fish it out of a box.

Gone are the days of keeping seven assault rifles, ten SMGs, and four rocket launchers in your back pocket—you can only equip two "long" guns on your back, and large melee weapons like bats have to be stowed away, too. Aside from how cool it is to fish a shotgun out of my trunk like a disgruntled Jason Statham character, the limitation is forcing me to think twice about how to approach missions.

And unlike in Red Dead's lawless towns, the NPCs of Leonida seem to react negatively to the guy walking around with assault rifles on his back. The game tells you early on that police pay closer attention to you when openly carrying firearms—another reason to stow them away when you don't need 'em.

Sources indicate that the car trunk is also where extra outfits can be stored. You can bring along five by default (more than Red Dead's saddles allowed), and even this isn't just for vanity. GTA 6's wanted system goes further than police chases: if you lose the cops, your wanted level will linger and cops identify you based on your description, clothes, and your car. The easiest way to go incognito after raising cain is to pull over, pop the trunk, and change outfits.

Keep up to date with the most crucial stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

It's all very smart and cool and I love it. Though I can also understand why others wouldn't—it's a significant break from what GTA has been up to this point. The two gun limit means murderous rampages might end earlier than they used to, and I can foresee getting annoyed the first time I bring a sniper rifle to a shotgun fight and have no way to correct that. But I think this reflects how Rockstar designed GTA 6 to be just as much a life sim as a crime fantasy.

Industry observers note that GTA 6 wants me to constantly make choices and consider what a real human would do. Like in one mission last night, I was left alone without my personal vehicle for the first time. Instead of Rockstar suggesting I grand theft an auto, a tutorial popped for calling a cab. So yea, I took a yellow cab back to my car a few miles away, and it was a chill ride, except for the cabbie who rudely shot down my attempts to make small talk. He's lucky my guns were in my car.

📖 Baca
Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: The Apple Watch's New 'Siri Recap' Feature Is Even Creepier Than I Expected

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1368 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the “Siri Recap” feature that Apple confirmed in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on.
  • Industry observers note that I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything.
  • In a recent development, the recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the “Siri Recap” feature that Apple confirmed in September is finally available in a developer beta, and I’ve spent the last 24 hours with the feature turned on. It’s even more unsettling than the “Live Rewind” feature that introduced at the same time. It listens to all my conversations, and produces summaries that are both helpful and deeply creepy.

Industry observers note that I have a button in the watch’s Control Center that can turn the recapping abilities off, but if I forget to do so, Siri listens to everything. I’ll get a recap of my entire evening, presented in roughly hour-long chunks, including things I would have completely forgotten I had even heard about.

In a recent development, the recaps somberly mention silly memes my kids were laughing about, and make major bullet points out of offhand remarks from brief conversations. If a conversation sticks to a single topic, I’ll often get a reasonably good summary of it, with specific facts and numbers highlighted; but just as often, Siri will get confused and mix up several topics or completely mishear a name or phrase.

Apple has four features that it considers part of “audio intelligence":.

Music recognition, better known as Shazam. We’ve had a version of this on the Apple Watch for a long time now, although it has some improvements and now identifies music automatically.

Sources indicate that sound recognition, which can notify you about doorbells and babies crying. A version of this introduced in 2020 as an accessibility feature.

Live Rewind, which gives you an on-wrist transcript of the last 15 seconds of detected speech.

Siri Recaps, which summarizes entire conversations for you to read on your phone.

Live Rewind had the flashiest demo from the Apple event: A server rattled off the day’s specials at a restaurant, and then the Apple Watch-wearing diner checked his watch to see a readout of exactly which dishes had just been mentioned. The utility is both obvious and kind of unnecessary: Why wouldn’t you just ask the server to repeat the list while they’re standing right there?

I haven’t found myself using Live Rewind, except out of curiosity about how the feature works. I discovered that it doesn’t pick up song lyrics very well, and also that by the time I think to check what was just said in a conversation, more than 15 seconds has passed since the part I was unsure about. I haven’t yet found a reason to use it for real.

But Siri Recaps? Those are both useful and unsettling. I enabled the feature, and decided to test it out later. But since it was on, it dutifully listened in as I picked up my son from school and gave him an update on an ailing family member’s health. We stopped by the library, and along the way we chatted about a variety of things: holiday travel plans, library policies, and the possibility of humans living in space in the future. Siri was listening to it all.

Sources indicate that after you're updated to 27.3, go into the Watch app, tap Siri, and turn on Siri Recap. You can set a schedule for when it should listen (for example, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., if you want it on for the work day but off for the evening). You'll need to set a passcode on your watch, and you'll be guided through a step to upgrade your audio connection. The control center on the watch will have a button you can use to turn Siri recaps on and off at will. To read your recaps, go to the Siri app on your phone.

As promised, the recaps do not identify speakers. They do not contain an exact transcript, and there is no way to listen to a recording to check what exactly was mentioned. This is probably good for privacy and for relationships; there’s no way to prove that your spouse said such-and-such exact thing. I can also tell people I am not recording them, and technically be correct.

But still: I feel weird publishing the contents of these recaps, because they do contain things that people remarked to me in what they assumed was a private setting. I had the feature on when I attended a choir practice, and Siri recapped the brief chats I had with other choir members before and after practice. (Interestingly, it did not recap any of the quiet conversations I had with fellow sopranos while the tenors were rehearsing their part. I’m not sure if the watch was unable to hear us over the music, or if Siri is programmed not to listen when music is being played.).

Industry observers note that because speakers aren’t identified, it seems Siri doesn’t know what to do when there is a disagreement. A human note-taker would jot down that Person A made a point in favor of something, and person B made a point against. But when my son and I disagreed about how likely space colonization might be in the future, the recap didn’t reflect the separate positions that were put forth. It summarized the conversation as including “debating the feasibility and timeline of human space colonization and asteroid mining,” which isn’t exactly accurate, but close enough.

Sources indicate that when it comes to the content of the discussion, the recap notes a bullet point of “skepticism regarding permanent space colonies within the next 100 years.” It didn’t include my reasons for being skeptical, and didn’t mention my son’s opposing viewpoint at all. If I were using this recap to jog my memory of the conversation, it wouldn’t be all that helpful.

It has been revealed that details are sometimes egregiously incorrect. After a discussion about a family member’s health, the recap had notes on the prognosis of “father.” The family member we discussed is not anybody’s father. Names in general seem to be a problem; I recommended a book to my son, and the recap includes notes about the content of the book, but not its title. The book’s author appears in the introduction to the recap (sort of a summary of a summary), but not in the content of the recap itself where the book is mentioned.

Industry observers note that I should probably turn Siri recaps off. It seems wrong to let people chat with me without letting them know that their conversation is being ... well, not technically recorded, but basically recorded.

In a recent development, but it’s so tempting to leave it on so that I can review my day. Some of the details in the recaps are useful, like the dates that were discussed as options for a holiday party. The recaps will be deleted in about a week (unless I save them to the notes app), so if I want to remind myself of a conversation a few days ago, I should be able to scroll back through my recaps and find it.

It has been revealed that I would be a fool to rely on the recaps, though. The most notable points of a conversation are often left out; Siri doesn’t know what’s actually important, and there’s no way to guide it as to what to pay attention to. Specific details can be wrong, as I mentioned. There’s also no way to control when a “conversation” starts or stops, unless you are turning the recap feature on and off from the watch.

And there’s more: Not only are names usually omitted (wait, who did she say I should ask about that project?), the few identifiers that make it into the recap, like names of events, are often wrong. Subjects of discussion are often conflated in really unhelpful ways: My husband mentioned paying for certain course registrations for one of our children, and later I talked to that child about an unrelated exam. The recap got all of these things mixed up with each other and was wrong about pretty much every detail. About all the recap could usefully do is to remind me that something about AP U.S. History was discussed. Reading the recaps can be like reliving your day entirely in the passive voice.

PlayStation defeats £2 billion UK lawsuit that alleged Sony forced consumers into "excessive and unfair prices"

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (478 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness).
  • The case, brought by Alex Neill, who mentioned she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store.
  • "Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value users who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that sony has defeated a major £2 billion UK class action lawsuit concerning the price of games on the PlayStation Store (thanks, TheGameBusiness). The judgment came after a 30-day Competition Appeal Tribunal that took place in London, where PlayStation customers claimed Sony had removed "all actual and potential competition" in relation to selling digital games on the console.

The case, brought by Alex Neill, who mentioned she represented roughly 12.2 million gamers, accused Sony of applying "excessive and unfair" pricing on games that appeared on the storefront accessible by PS3, PS4 and PS5 consoles - the PlayStation Store. In a judgment published by the London’s Competition Appeal Tribunal today (17th November), the case was rejected. The judgement noted that market definitions used to define Sony's conduct were "unsafe", and that consumers "would be likely to make informed choices when purchasing consoles" and games on the hardware, too.

"Potential PlayStation console purchasers had both access to sufficient information and an incentive to consider that information in order to make informed purchasing decisions at the console level, especially in the case of high-value users who spend significant amounts in the digital gaming aftermarket," read the judgment.

According to recent reports, the lawsuit made the argument that, upon purchasing a PS5 or other PlayStation console, you were then trapped within its ecosystem, and forced into paying the prices determined by Sony. The Tribunal disagreed, however, and ruled that Sony competed within a wider 'systems market' alongside Xbox, Nintendo and PC, for example. Furthermore, the Tribunal found no evidence that the existence of other digital storefronts would have actually brought any PlayStation Store pricing down.

Interestingly, the Tribunal used the argument that consumers can also opt and buy physical games instead of using the PlayStation Store - something that is changing as of the start of 2028. That did not seem to have any bearing on today's decision, though. It's also worth noting that this case did not seek to interrogate the ownership status of digital games - something that's been at the heart of the movement rallying against Sony's decision to kill off physical media. Earlier this year, spokespeople from Sony's legal team argued "reasonable consumers" already know they don't actually own their digital games.

The London Tribunal has a fairly long history. Back in 2022, it began as a case that attempted to sue Sony to the tune of £5bn for "ripping people off" on PlayStation Store. Sony argued the case brought against it in this trial was "flawed from start to finish". This isn't the only situation where we're seeing consumers pursue legal action against the platform holder. Last year, PlayStation was sued in the Netherlands over the so-called "Sony tax" that highlighted artificially inflated prices on the Store, and sought to represent more than 20,000 participants that felt short-changed by the organization.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that knowing how to workout in GTA 6 will help you to increase your Strength and Cardio, which in turn will improve your health and increase your stamina. Working out will also manage your weight and build up muscle, affecting your appearance in GTA 6. While fancy gym memberships all over Leonida will become available in time, Jason has everything needed to get a sweat on right outside his house from the beginning of the story.

According to recent reports, realism is key here, so you can't just spend all day crunching weights as you'll soon hit a wall where no further gains can be made until you rest and recover – though consuming some protein after will halve the time you need to wait before you can go again. On screen prompts will inform you when you reach that point, and you can check the Fitness app on your phone to see what your current status and stats are. If you want to get fit fast, here's how to workout in GTA 6.

The lower deck area behind Jason's house is full of Strength workout equipment, so this is a great place to start building muscle. If you're still in the process of repairing the property, then this is also where to fix the railing in GTA 6. To start exercising with any of the equipment, walk up to it and follow the prompt.

Most of the Strength workouts in GTA 6 follow the same basic method – hold both triggers to lift the weight (or yourself), then gradually release the triggers to lower back down in a controlled way, before fully pushing in both trigger to repeat the process. You shouldn't rush this, but keep an eye on your stamina gauge in the top-left corner as if that fully depletes then your workout will end. You may also need to quickly press X/A to push out the last few difficult reps, so watch out for that prompt too.

Kettlebell swings in GTA 6 are not like the other Strength workouts, as instead of carefully lowering the weight you need to let it drop freely then start your next swing at just the right time to maintain the momentum into the following rep. Look for the point where the kettlebell is between your legs and almost as far back as it will go, then squeeze both triggers to swing it back up to the top again before letting go.

In a recent development, while most of the early GTA 6 workouts you can do at Jason's house are Strength-based, there is a way to build your Cardio here too. Head to the back of the workshop underneath the house and you'll see a HANG BAG prompt appear, so hold that button to set up your punching bag outside.

Industry observers note that unlike the Strength exercises that you have to interact with to begin, you can simply walk up to the punching bag and start pressing the Melee button to rain down hits on it. No progress bar or rep counter will appear, though you'll get a notification when your Cardio gains have been maxed out for the time being.

While this isn't a specific workout activity in GTA 6, you can also increase your Cardio by running or swimming for a period of time. A notification will appear to confirm this, but remember to check the Fitness app as if you've already maxed out your current Cardio gains then running all over the place won't give you further improvement.

As well as looking after your physical health, make sure you work on your GTA 6 relationship status to keep things sweet between Lucia and Jason.

Of course, the roses represent the infamous enchanted rose that serves as the ticking time clock for the Beast in the 1991 animated classic.

It has been revealed that the rose appliqués are definitely the stars of the dress. Their coral, salmon, and deep red colors pop against the glittery white of the gown. There are also a smattering of smaller blossoms decorated throughout, tying the whole dress together. And the back is just as stunning as the front, with an elegant train featuring the same roses and delicate white buttons down the back of the bodice. It might not be as iconic as the animated film’s yellow gown, but it’s still more than fit for a princess.

In addition to dazzling the crowd, Chabert also filmed a “get-ready-with-me” video with the official Disney Wedding’s Instagram page, where she shared some of her favorite Christmas memories and revealed that Belle is her favorite princess. So, this look really was a dream for her.

In a recent development, honestly, the movie premiere and Belle-inspired dress could not have come at a more perfect time, considering Beauty and the Beast is gearing up to celebrate its 35th anniversary on November 22. And just a few days later, on November 28, fans will get to see Chabert's brand fresh Disney World Hallmark movie, Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True.

Filmed on Disney World property last year, the movie will follow Lindsey (Chabert) and her extended family as they head to ‘The Most Magical Place on Earth” to celebrate Christmas. However, the magic is short-lived when she discovers that their next-door neighbor is Philip (Travis Van Winkle), a guy she went on a disastrous first date with.

After the awkward reunion, Lindsey decides to make a wish at Cinderella’s wishing well for a love that’s “right out of a fairytale.” She might not think Philip is her Prince Charming, but as their paths continue to cross, they realize they have a lot more in common than their disastrous first date led on.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Holiday Ever After: A Disney World Wish Come True is one of the most anticipated films of Hallmark’s Countdown to Christmas lineup, and you won’t want to miss it. If you do miss its premiere on the cable channel, you can catch it streaming the next day with a Hallmark+ or Disney+ subscription.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware.
  • The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As you've probably heard, GTA 6 is out on consoles this week and targeting 30 FPS on that hardware. Despite reports claiming one may not be far away, there's still no official word on a PC port, hence why we've not got a review that delves deep into analysis of just how central to the experience the smell reaction system is.

The wait for confirmation of a PC version continues, then, and it looks like that might well be the only chance people get to play the crime sandbox at 60fps, with Rockstar having confirmed that higher frame rate modes aren't en-route to even the most beefy of consoles.

Speaking to Kotaku, GTA 6's devs made clear optional 60 or 40fps performance modes aren't on the way, even for the more powerful Pro variant of the PS5.

"Our base presentation makes use of ray-traced reflections and global illumination. On the PS5 Pro, this is enhanced with the addition of ray-traced shadows, as well as overall added clarity through the use of PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR)," Rockstar technology production director Marc Chambers put it. "The PS5 Pro features an upgraded graphics processor and upscaling technology that we leverage to increase the game’s visual fidelity. While the PS5 Pro’s central processor is slightly better than the PS5 base console, it is not powerful enough to run the game’s complex simulation at higher frame rates.".

So, there you go. The consoles just ain't got that dog in 'em. One would think, then, that being able to run GTA 6 in all its glory at higher frame rates will likely be a selling point for that PC port that's assumed to be on the way. Whether the average PC owner's graphics card and other bits will have the horses to deliver a smooth 60 is another question, and an especially pertinent one given the ongoing RAM crisis has made upgrading certain aspects of your setup ludicrously expensive.

If it requires a 5090 at a minimum, I guess those of us with less than absolute cutting edge cards will just have to keep playing Sleeping Dogs until the AI bubble bursts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’re playing GTA 6 and finding it too dark, there’s a good chance you may have your HDR calibration wrong – and no, it’s not your fault!

An extensive research video by HDTV Test – performed on a pricey Sony reference monitor – reveals the game’s HDR calibration may not be working quite as intended.

So while you may have followed the steps perfectly, setting your values until the Rockstar logo is only just visible as instructed, it may not be displaying optimally in your game.

I’d recommend you watch HDTV Test’s video for the full scientific analysis, but in short he explains that the various values in the HDR calibration settings output unexpectedly in-game.

Furthermore, the Rockstar release completely ignores Sony’s global PS5 HDR settings, so while you may have those calibrated perfectly for your particular screen, that won’t help you here.

Here’s how to fix it on PS5, according to HDTV Test – although do keep in mind your optimal personal settings will depend on your display, room, and preferred ambient lighting.

Load the game and press Options > Settings > Display > HDR Calibration.

HDTV Test recommends ignoring Rockstar’s own brightness calibration, so don’t worry too much if the company’s iconic logo is visible or not.

Instead focus on the two sample images of the party on the boat, which you can toggle between light and dark using R1.

These are the recommended starting settings for a display capable of 1,000 nits or higher:.

Feel free to tune these to taste; your own optimal HDR calibration settings will depend on your environment and screen, after all.

But this should help with the overall appearance of the game, and ensure you’re able to see a little bit better in the dark.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manni L. Perez has been confirmed as the actress behind Grand Theft Auto 6's Lucia Caminos, just days before the game releases.

As spotted by IGN, the confirmation came during The Game Awards' nominations livestream today, where Perez was nominated for Best Performance for her role as co-lead Lucia.

Perez had been widely rumoured to play Lucia for months, and fans have regularly filled her social media livestreams with questions about GTA 6, which she has been oh-so-carefully sidestepping.

Lucia is one half of GTA 6's lead pair alongside Jason Duval, making it the first Grand Theft Auto game with a playable couple.

Jason's actor wasn't among the nominees, so who plays him is still a mystery.

Perez has previously had guest roles in a string of US TV dramas, including Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago P.D., The Blacklist, and Blindspot, and has also done voice work for GTA Online.

Funnily enough, Lucia isn't her first Lucia - she also played Lucia Santiago in a 2023 episode of CBS's East Newly introduced York.

GTA 6 arrives 19th November on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It is now available to pre-load for anyone who pre-ordered the digital version, and those with the code-in-box physical version.

It's long been revealed that GTA 6 will have a regional release, meaning that some lucky, soon-to-be players will be able to access the game much earlier than others. Rockstar's regional release schedule sees the game launching at midnight on 19th November regardless of what region you're in, and if you wish to join those playing almost a day early, there's the good ol' Xbox New Zealand trick for eager players to try.

How to find Bigfoot, or Mr. Mangrove the Skunk Ape, in GTA 6

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bigfoot in GTA 6, also known as Skunk Ape or Mr Mangrove, isn't just an Easter egg, but a full blown chain of side quests tied to a character called Kirk, who's obsessively hunting the cryptid through the Floridian swamp.
  • According to recent reports, to start with you'll have to ensure your random encounter with the Skunk Ape, but afterwards you can pursue the quest line pretty straightforwardly.
  • For a friendlier form of wildlife, check out how to pet animals in GTA 6.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bigfoot in GTA 6, also known as Skunk Ape or Mr Mangrove, isn't just an Easter egg, but a full blown chain of side quests tied to a character called Kirk, who's obsessively hunting the cryptid through the Floridian swamp. After your character stumbles across Bigfoot's location, you can contact Kirk and help him hunt down the Skunk Ape for good across several missions, in which you find the strange effigies that this creature is leaving behind. All this wraps up with a fairly significant choice, one that harkens back somewhat to the famous bigfoot encounter in Red Dead Redemption.

According to recent reports, to start with you'll have to ensure your random encounter with the Skunk Ape, but afterwards you can pursue the quest line pretty straightforwardly. Pick the right choices, and you can get a real cash reward.

For a friendlier form of wildlife, check out how to pet animals in GTA 6.

The Skunk Ape questline in which you help Kirk hunt down a monster he calls "Mister Mangrove" is broken up into several smaller quests and objectives.

Sources indicate that this is a questline you can start very early on in GTA 6, all the way in chapter 1 1, and see through to the end in the same chapter. The rewards are pretty significant, assuming you make a certain choice.

To find Bigfoot initially in GTA 6 before starting the Skunk Ape quest, you need to go to the location on the GTA 6 map marked above. Once there, you'll see Bigfoot moving fleeing into the marshland after eating a deer.

Industry observers note that it's not mandatory that you follow (or even that you have this encounter for the larger quest), but if you do, you'll be led to an effigy tied to a tree. Examining it for too long causes you to inhale spores from it and pass out.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

To start Kirk's quest "Skunk Apeology 101", go to the Rusty Anchor bar in North Key Lento. On entering through the main doors, look immediately to the right and examine the notice board. There'll be a poster left by Kirk, with a number to call if you've seen the Skunk Ape.

With the number added to your contacts, call Kirk. He'll give you a meeting place and time to start the quest, marked on your map with KK.

Meeting with Kirk and getting some explanatory dialogue, he'll have you hit a stick against a truck to trigger the distant howls of Mr. Mangrove. You'll follow him into the woods (I recommend you equip your flashlight in the equipment tab in the bottom left radial menu).

In a recent development, to find Mr. Mangrove after splitting up, use your Focus Mode when you hear the Skunk Ape howling, and there'll be a ripple effect. Follow those ripples until a chase is triggered, leading to another effigy.

At this point, after studying it, you'll be chased by a strange boar. Don't worry too much about escape – whether it catches you or not, you'll end up back at the car, either because you flee successfully or because you're knocked out and Kirk drags you there. He'll tell you he'll contact you again with the next steps, which will take about half a day in-game.

It has been revealed that kirk tells you that he needs you to find three tree Effigies left behind by Mr. Mangrove. There are actually nine of them in total, but you only need to find three of them. We've marked all their locations on the map above – when you're close, use Focus Mode again to see them through the trees, then use L2/LT to study them.

After completing this, you'll be given another message to wait, as now Kirk has the data needed to track the Skunk Ape down for good.

On meeting back up with Kirk at night, you'll be given a customised tranquilizer rifle and taken up in a helicopter. After flushing out the Skunk Ape, you need to fire several rounds into it. Despite the long range, there's no drop-off or delay on the rifle, so just aim at Mr. Mangrove's centre mass and you should be fine.

Recent findings suggest that eventually he'll end up in a small encampment. Follow him into the building, and you'll see him pass out. When you try to lift him however, things get weird, as you'll be exposed to the pollen spores he emanates and pass out.

Sources indicate that in this questionably hallucinatory experience, you'll now control a frog and have to find flies to eat. There are three different spots to go to where flies congregate over corpses.

In a recent development, be wary that there are alligators who will try to eat you. Keep your distance, and use Focus Mode to home in on the flies.

Having eaten flies, now you'll become one, obviously. Head back to the shack you found the Skunk Ape in, but now follow the other pier around back to the helicopter (its lights should mark it out). Stay close to Kirk, and you'll hear him talking about a man named Harry Sherrick who disappeared – who actually is Mr. Mangrove, with a valuable QR code tattoo that will lead to open his substantial bank account.

Waking up in the shack with Kirk and the unconscious Mr. Mangrove, you can choose to side with either of them, now knowing that Kirk is fully aware that the Skunk Ape is some transformed human being and is only hunting him to rob him. You can choose to shoot either of them with the dart gun, or neither. Here are the options and what they give you:.

Sources indicate that no matter what outcome you pick, you get to keep the rifle, a legendary variant "Mister Mangrove" Laird 350 Bolt Action Rifle. That reward, at least, is consistent.

Of the three, the best choice if you want to make money fast in GTA 6 is to shoot Mr. Mangrove. However, if you want to be an ethical criminal, I would shoot neither and let the Skunk Ape have his revenge.

According to recent reports, it's heavily implied that Mr. Mangrove is a man named Harry Sherrick who was transformed by swamp spores into a Skunk Ape, similar to the mutated boar that chases you early in the quest chain.

In a recent development, kirk knows this and has been relentlessly hunting and hounding Sherrick anyway – not to help him, or to reveal the truth to the world, but to simply get access to the tattoo and steal the money. Kirk's a pretty shitty person, simply put, especially as he had no intention of even cutting Jason and Lucia in on the reward.

If you lose track of your new rifle, make sure you know how to store and recover your weapons in GTA 6.

10 Hacks Every Reddit User Should Know

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that if you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit.
  • It has been revealed that reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private.
  • It has been revealed that old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you're looking for discussions, recommendations, or advice online, it's hard to avoid Reddit. From mainstream sports to niche crafts, it does seem that there's some kind of Reddit community for everyone. (And if there's not one, you can make one yourself.) If you're using Reddit, here are 10 hacks you should know about to improve your experience on the site.

It has been revealed that reddit used to let everyone view your post and comment history, but in recent years, you can make your profile private. You can hide your posts, comments, and the subreddits you're a part of. If you want to do this, click your profile icon once you've logged in to Reddit, and go to Settings > Profile. Alternatively, you can follow the direct link to Reddit's profile settings page. Click the drop-down menu next to Content & Activity, and select Hide all. You should also turn off Online Status on the same page to stop people from seeing when you're using Reddit.

It has been revealed that old Reddit lets you use the site's classic design, and I prefer it to the more modern UI. Old Reddit looks dated, but it doesn't have infinite scrolling, distracting animations, and a bunch of features designed to increase the time you spend on the platform. It's no wonder that Reddit is making it harder to access this version of the site. As long as it's around, you should switch to Old Reddit for a cleaner reading experience. You can do that by going to Reddit Settings > Preferences and enabling Default to Old Reddit. You can also visit old.reddit.com, though you'll need to sign in for access.

In a recent development, many subreddits use custom themes that range from beautiful to borderline unusable. If you want a more consistent UI across the site, you should disable these custom subreddit styles. Go to Reddit Settings > Preferences and turn off Use community themes. If you're using Old Reddit, click the preferences button in the top-right corner, and under "display options," disable allow subreddits to show me custom themes.

Reddit's social features are useful if you have friends on the site, but in most cases, those features are annoying at best. If your post or comment goes viral, be prepared to deal with waves of weirdos who find it entertaining to send unsolicited advice or opinions. To keep all of this at bay, you should disable the site's social features. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Allow people to follow you. On the same page, click Who can send you chat requests, and pick Nobody. You can also turn off Show up in search results to remove your profile from Google searches.

Industry observers note that A multireddit is a feed that indicates posts from a customized group of subreddits. You can think of it as a way to break out of Reddit's algorithms, and create your own Reddit feed. I use multireddits to follow all sports-related subs I'm interested in. I even have one for gaming, and one for fountain pens. It's a great way to create interest-specific feeds, and if you make them private, no one else can see them. To create one, click the Create custom feed button in the left pane in fresh Reddit. In the Old Reddit design, click the Create button in the left pane. Be sure to select the Private button to keep it from showing up for others. You can add as many subreddits as you like to the list, and bookmark the feed to access it whenever you wish to.

According to recent reports, if you want to reduce Reddit's tracking, you should turn off ad personalization. Go to Reddit Settings > Privacy, and turn off Personalize ads. To block Reddit's ads altogether, you can use any ad blocker you like. I recommend uBlock Origin, which is one of the best ad blockers you can install, though most can hide Reddit's ads on desktop. On mobile, you can try using AdGuard or Wipr to hide in-app ads in Reddit.

Reddit has recently adopted an Instagram-like experience for its feeds. It removed the ability to sort posts by new, controversial, best, etc., and instead offers "For You" and "Following." If you dislike this change, you can bypass it. I use Reddit on mobile Safari, and I recommend an extension called Sink It for Reddit. It can automatically redirect you to Old Reddit, and there's a feature that optimizes it for mobile, which brings back the old sorting options. You can also use third-party apps such as RedReader for Android, or RDX for Reddit on an iPhone or iPad to restore the old sorting options for Reddit posts.

Sources indicate that after all these years, Reddit's built-in search still leaves something to be desired—at least, on the surface. To find posts on Reddit faster, use search filters on the site. For instance, adding "title:" to your search will limit the results to post titles, and boolean operators such as AND, OR, and NOT also work for advanced searches on the site.

It has been revealed that one of GTA's many gags is back in GTA 6: the ol' bigfoot sighting. Well, technically I think it's a "skunk ape," real-life Florida's maybe real-life boogeyman "cousin" to Bigfoot. Don't get that cryptid family tree twisted. How do I know it's skunk ape? I saw the thing, I swear, and there was a cloud of green stink wafting off of it. Here's exactly where it's at if you want your own smelly primate encounter.

It has been revealed that the skunk ape sighting I've found so far is just across Gambit Bay from Jason's initial house. Hop in Jason's boat on the dock outside his place and set course for the dead end road on the inside of this peninsula. Before you even make land you'll get a prompt telling you to use Focus Mode to follow the source of the noises.

Hark! It's skunk ape! The creature hightails its stinky hide off into the mangrove-y woods and you'll need to keep using focus mode to chase after. You'll lose sight of it and instead find some creepy effigy thing standing beside a tree. Check it out, get stink-apacitated, and get your not so informative close-up sighting of bigfoot's big feet.

After your sighting, keep your eyes peeled for flyers about the skunk ape posted on storefronts and telephone poles around Leonida. They'll lead you to a mission where you can learn more about the mysterious beast.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games.
  • It has been revealed that in development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time.
  • The original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that goat Simulator and Satisfactory outfit Coffee Stain Group have bought the intellectual property rights and assets for Chronicles: Medieval, the Tom Hardy-garnished strategy RPG that was originally in development at now-bankrupt Raw Power Games. The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

It has been revealed that in development since 2022, and slated for Steam early access release in 2027, Chronicles: Medieval is a game about building vast armies of men in metal hats and horrifying doublets, then fighting alongside them in real time. It sees you positioning archers behind spears and finessing your cavalry flanking actions, all the while occupying a fleshy human body that can be hacked and stabbed. It's set during the Hundred Years' War between England and France over the 14th and 15th centuries, and gives you a volatile sandbox world of warring factions and patrols.

The original devs included people who worked on The Witcher 3, Total War, and Crusader Kings III, which may not surprise you from the foregoing descriptions. It's not entirely clear who has made the leap to Coffee Stain's newly founded studio.

It has been revealed that raw Power declared bankruptcy on 30th October, subsequently calling on players to help them find funding. During the bankruptcy proceedings, Coffee Stain successfully bid 36.75 million Danish Krone for Chronicles: Medieval, which comes to around four million pounds or 5.4 million dollars. According to CEO Anton Westbergh the project "ticks many of the boxes that we believe to be fundamental for a great game, and we think it has a good chance of becoming a strong long-term IP for the group." The game yet sits at 26th on SteamDB's most wishlisted, despite Raw Power's funding troubles.

Gaming doesn't want for simulations of shrieking feudal folk, but Medieval has a certain swagger, even when you remove Tom Hardy from the picture (and you should - he only ever voiced that one trailer). Here's hoping the fresh team can find their feet under Coffee Stain, and that whoever hasn't made the transition finds good work elsewhere.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even though it feels like NCIS: Origins just premiered on the 2026 TV schedule, the series is already winding down its third season. Along with a few other CBS highlights, Origins’ season was cut short due to scheduling. Instead of a full season, it’s only getting ten episodes and will be replaced by NCIS: Sydney in January, which is also getting just ten episodes. Now, with the Season 3 finale fast approaching, Kyle Schmid is very passionate about getting a Season 4 renewal, but his words don’t exactly reassure me.

In a recent development, the NCIS prequel is only three seasons in, but it’s definitely become a favorite among fans. And with Mark Harmon back as Leroy Jethro Gibbs for all of Season 3, these fresh episodes are better than ever. And the hope for a fourth season is getting stronger. Unfortunately, there’s no telling when CBS could be making a decision, so Schmid is jumping on the campaign train. The Mike Franks actor told TV Insider just how much the show, crew, and cast deserve another season, and I desperately need it:.

The show is exceptional this year. I’m so proud of the writing team, our cast, our crew, everybody that I had the pleasure of working with for the past four or five months. I think we found our thing this year. I think the show’s found its shape. I think the characters have found their meaning.

As a day one Origins fan, I would love nothing more than to never see this show end, especially because it’s gotten better the longer it’s been on. Even with fewer episodes, Origins has been pumping out some great storylines, and that’s going to continue until the very end of Season 3. Plus, while Schmid couldn’t go into detail about what’s to come, his comments make it clear that Origins cannot end any time soon:.

And let me tell you, when I say I don’t want the show to end like this, the show can’t end like this, and I mean that with all my fucking heart. So when you get to the finale of the show, you will know damn well what I mean when I say it cannot go out like this, so there better be a Season fucking 4.

This has me very concerned, because Schmid is implying that we're going to be dying to see what happens after Season 3 ends. And let me tell you, I absolutely hate cliffhangers, and I hold grudges against them when shows are canceled right after one, because I know we'll never get a resolution. So, if Origins ends in a way that leaves me ravenous for more, it better not get axed.

Now, I can't say I'm shocked that we probably need to prepare for a brutal cliffhanger. If NCIS: Origins is great at one thing, it’s ending seasons on them. Season 1’s finale saw Lala getting into a car crash, while Season 2 ended with Randy getting abducted. If Season 3 follows the pattern and ends on a cliffhanger, which it sounds like it will, a cancellation would be heartbreaking.

CBS has confirmed that the Season 3 finale of NCIS: Origins will premiere on January 19, so fans will see just what Schmid is talking about in two months. I am also passionate about the show getting another season, and if the finale is as massive as it sounds, I will be hopping on the campaign train with the actor.

For now, fans will just have to wait and see what happens. The series is at the moment off for the Thanksgiving holiday, but newly introduced episodes will be back on Tuesday, December 1, on CBS, streaming the next day with a Paramount+ subscription.

10 Hacks Every Hulu User Should Know

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, if you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations.
  • Another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain demonstrates.
  • Sources indicate that if you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you don't like the content Hulu is suggesting for you, you have several options to curate your recommendations. "Disliking" a show or movie removes it from your Home view and You May Also Like entirely, so the only way you'll see that content is if you search for it. You can dislike on the Details page if you're watching on your TV or use the thumbs down on mobile or web. (The "Like" button will obviously influence your algorithm in the opposite way). If your "Continue Watching" queue is cluttered with shows you started but didn't like enough to finish, you can remove them from your watch history as well as the My Stuff list. This, too, will allow content to remain searchable but not suggested in other areas of the app.

Another approach to protecting your profile and algorithm is to set up separate profiles for specific use cases, such as when you have guests or if you host watch parties for certain demonstrates. This keeps content from influencing your recommendations and prevents other viewers from seeing what's in your watch history or saved content (especially if there are things you want to keep private).

Sources indicate that if you find that subtitles and captions are too bold—or not visible enough—you can change the font, color, size, and style from the default so they enhance your viewing experience rather than detracting from it. Hulu allows you to adjust the color and opacity of the font, background, and window so you get the right contrast, and you can also select the specific font and font scaling. On your streaming device, go to Settings > Subtitles & Captions, then hit the back button on your remote to save your preferences. You can update these settings on mobile and desktop as well.

If you have a long list of demonstrates and films to watch but can't decide what to start next, look for the "Expiring Soon" badge to see which titles are leaving the service in the next two weeks. Badges display the number of days remaining, so you can determine what to prioritize and whether it's worth diving in based on how much time you have to finish before the expiration date. Go to "My Stuff" to monitor saved titles that are expiring soon.

Industry observers note that if you've been watching Hulu under an account shared with family or friends and need to switch to your own subscription, you can transfer your profile to keep your watch history and settings intact instead of starting from scratch. You can initiate a profile transfer on a TV-connected device. Note that account holders have to approve transfer requests within seven days, and once expired, transfer requests cannot be resubmitted—so be sure to let the primary user know that you've made the request.

In a recent development, if you've shared your Hulu login information with friends or activated your account on devices you don't own, you may want to regularly audit where your account is being used and remove any that don't need access. This includes TVs in Airbnbs and hotels. If you stay logged in, unauthorized users may have access to your Hulu account and personal data. You can see activated devices (and their activation date) under Your Account > Watch Hulu on Your Devices > Manage Devices. Click Remove next to old or unrecognized devices.

According to recent reports, hulu has an offline mode that allows you to download highlights and movies to watch when you don't have a network connection. This is useful for traveling or when you know your wifi or cell service will be limited. Downloads are only available on supported iOS and Android devices, which means you may have to consider how much space your content takes up. You can select High for video quality if you want maximum resolution, but you may want to choose Standard if you are short on storage. This option is available under Downloads > Settings > Video Quality on iOS and Account > Settings > Downloads > Video Quality on Android. Note that once you click play on downloaded content, you have 48 hours to watch it before it expires—so don't start it unless you are ready.

Sources indicate that if you have a Hulu + Live TV subscription, you must designate a "Home" network, which determines the local channels included in your plan. You can update your location up to four times within a 12-month period, but this limitation is meant to prevent viewers outside a household from sharing a subscription. Hulu does allow you to stream live TV on mobile when you're away from your home network (within the U.S.) as long as you access your account on that network every 30 days. If you travel often, check in with your mobile device frequently to avoid being locked out when you're away. Note that you can still watch streaming content with no restrictions.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.
  • Recent findings suggest that the cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter.
  • Recent findings suggest that its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Civilization and XCOM developer Firaxis Games has laid off around 60 people.

Recent findings suggest that the cuts, which took place today, account for about a third of the studio’s staff, Bloomberg reports, citing people familiar with the matter. Studio head Heather Hazen is also leaving.

Recent findings suggest that its sources say Firaxis' unannounced XCOM game has faced development struggles and missed "a significant milestone over the summer". The project will continue, but "may face a shakeup as a result of the cuts".

A spokesperson for 2K, the Take-Two label that runs Firaxis, confirmed Hazen's departure to Bloomberg, and mentioned the studio is "restructuring and recentering around the studio's core strength - designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years".

It has been revealed that "As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis," the spokesperson continued. "These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.".

The layoffs come two days before the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which is developed and published by Rockstar, a separate label at Take-Two.

In September, around 18 months after Civ 7's widely criticised launch - and as the legendary 4X series celebrates its 35th anniversary - Firaxis unveiled a host of latest updates coming to the game as it continued to improve it. These included an atomic age upgrade, dragging Civ 7 into the present and beyond, as well as its first paid expansion, Earthrise, both arriving next year.

Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick admitted earlier this year that the studio "got it wrong with Civ 7".

According to recent reports, "The game is a really good game. And it's certainly a profitable enterprise for us. But this is one where I think what we tried to do was a bridge too far, from the consumer's perspective," he told Game File in May.

It’s not the first round of cuts at the studio - 2K confirmed an unspecified number of layoffs at Firaxis in September 2025, and around 30 jobs went in 2023.
